steps.text: Rain. Not a storm. Just cold, steady, patient rain.

steps.title: Backstreet
steps.quote: A narrow street of shuttered shops.

steps.title: The vending machine
steps.quote: A vending machine hums on the corner.

steps.text: A narrow street of shuttered shops. A vending machine hums on the corner. High up, one lit window, a radio playing behind it.

steps.title: Mara walks
steps.quote: MARA VOSS (24) walks fast, arms folded, soaked, no umbrella.

steps.title: Mara's phone
steps.quote: Her phone lights up: VERA. She watches it ring.

steps.text: MARA VOSS (24) walks fast, arms folded, soaked, no umbrella. Her phone lights up: VERA. She watches it ring.
Not tonight.

steps.title: Not tonight
steps.quote: She declines it.

steps.text: She declines it.
THE SCRAP

steps.title: The scrap
steps.quote: The note in her hands. Her handwriting, in biro: 1.00 Sakai.

steps.text: The note in her hands. Her handwriting, in biro: 1.00 Sakai. Underneath is an address. Beneath that, underlined twice: "just listen."

steps.title: Down the lane
steps.quote: She looks down the lane. At the far end, the bar sign. She checks her watch (12.45). Early.

steps.text: She looks down the lane. At the far end, the bar sign. She checks her watch (12.45). Early.

steps.title: Barbershop doorway
steps.quote: She slips into the barbershop doorway, behind the scooter and the crates, and presses back into the shadow to shelter from the rain.

steps.text: The rain thickens. She slips into the barbershop doorway, behind the scooter and the crates, and presses back into the shadow to shelter from the rain. The beer crates will hide her from anyone in the lane. She hopes. She isn't sure she wants to walk in at all.

steps.title: The empty lane
steps.quote: Somewhere nearby, a pedestrian crossing CHIMES its old melody for an empty intersection.

steps.text: Somewhere nearby, a pedestrian crossing CHIMES its old melody for an empty intersection. Over and over. No one crosses.
Footsteps. Hurried. Uneven.

steps.title: Old man
steps.quote: An OLD MAN (70s) in a cheap raincoat and a grey flat cap comes in from the road, one hand pressed to his side as if something is hidden there.

steps.text: An OLD MAN (70s) in a cheap raincoat and a grey flat cap comes in from the road, one hand pressed to his side as if something is hidden there. He keeps looking back.
Mara sees him. Looks at the scrap.

steps.title: The red clip
steps.quote: She leans out of the shadow. The red bird clip catches the street light.

steps.text: She leans out of the shadow. The red bird clip catches the street light.

steps.title: Old man stops
steps.quote: He sees it. He stops, six metres short of her. For one second his whole face changes.

steps.text: He sees it. He stops, six metres short of her. For one second his whole face changes.

steps.title: He refuses
steps.quote: Then he shakes his head. Barely. A man refusing a stranger. And he turns his back on her, slowly, to face the road.

steps.text: Then he shakes his head. Barely. A man refusing a stranger. And he turns his back on her, slowly, to face the road.

steps.title: The sedan blocks the lane
steps.quote: Behind him, at the mouth of the lane, headlights. A black sedan pulls across the opening and stops, blocking it.

steps.text: Behind him, at the mouth of the lane, headlights. A black sedan pulls across the opening and stops, blocking it. Its high beams shine straight down the lane, lighting the rain in long white columns.
Two MEN get out and walk in, black silhouettes against the glare. Black clothes. Masks. They don't run.

steps.title: The white light
steps.quote: The old man doesn't move. He stands between them and Mara's doorway, a small figure in the white light, his shadow stretching long down the lane toward her.

steps.text: The old man doesn't move. He stands between them and Mara's doorway, a small figure in the white light, his shadow stretching long down the lane toward her.
After twenty years.

steps.title: The shot
steps.quote: A suppressed SHOT. Flat and ordinary, like a door closing.

steps.text: A suppressed SHOT. Flat and ordinary, like a door closing.
The old man folds onto the street.

steps.title: First position done
steps.quote: One of the masked men touches his ear.

steps.text: One of the masked men touches his ear.
First position done. Moving to second.

steps.title: Tail-lights gone
steps.quote: They walk back to the sedan. They don't hurry.

steps.text: They walk back to the sedan. They don't hurry. They never look at the doorway. It pulls away and takes the long way round the block, its high beams swinging off the lane.

steps.title: She kneels
steps.quote: Mara runs to the old man. Her bag slides off her shoulder and spills across the wet street. She doesn't notice.

steps.text: Mara runs to the old man. Her bag slides off her shoulder and spills across the wet street. She doesn't notice.
Mr. Sakai?
It's okay — I'll get someone — Ambulance. I'll call. Ambulance.

steps.title: The grip
steps.quote: His hand comes out of his coat with something small and brass in it. He presses it into her palm and closes her fingers over it.

steps.text: His hand comes out of his coat with something small and brass in it. He presses it into her palm and closes her fingers over it.
Don't let them have it.
Have what? I don't —
He's gone. Rain in his open eyes.

steps.title: The key
steps.quote: In her hand: a small brass key on a stamped number tag.

steps.text: In her hand: a small brass key on a stamped number tag.

steps.title: She runs
steps.quote: At the other end of the street, the amber glow of a bar. Mara runs for it.

steps.text: At the other end of the street, the amber glow of a bar. Mara runs for it.

steps.title: Her bag in the rain
steps.quote: Behind her, on the street: her purse, open in the rain.

steps.text: Behind her, on the street: her purse, open in the rain.

steps.title: The bar
steps.quote: Six stools and a counter. Shelves of bottles glowing amber.

steps.text: Six stools and a counter. Shelves of bottles glowing amber. On a high shelf, an old CRT television plays a late-night variety show, sound low. Rain drums on the roof.

steps.title: The journalist
steps.quote: A man in a raincoat on the far stool, a notebook beside a beer gone flat: the JOURNALIST (40s).

steps.text: A man in a raincoat on the far stool, a notebook beside a beer gone flat: the JOURNALIST (40s). Nobody behind the counter. Crates clatter somewhere in the back.

steps.title: Mara bursts in
steps.quote: Mara bursts in, the key in her fist.

steps.text: Mara bursts in, the key in her fist.
Miss Voss?

steps.title: He knows her name
steps.quote: He knows her name.

steps.title: Two pairs of shoes
steps.quote: Before she can answer, the door opens behind her. Rain noise.

steps.text: He knows her name. Before she can answer, the door opens behind her. Rain noise.
Shitsurei shimasu.

steps.title: Behind the counter
steps.quote: Mara is behind the counter before she knows she's moved.

steps.text: Mara is behind the counter before she knows she's moved.

steps.title: From the floor
steps.quote: Where is he?

steps.text: Where is he?

steps.title: The variety show
steps.quote: Two shots. On the high shelf, the television audience laughs.

steps.text: Two shots. On the high shelf, the television audience laughs.

steps.title: Clip under the shelf
steps.quote: A hair clip slides out of her wet hair and skitters under the shelf. She doesn't breathe.

steps.text: Behind the counter, Mara folds herself into the gap between the crates and the ice bin. A hair clip slides out of her wet hair and skitters under the shelf. She doesn't breathe.
Second position done.

steps.title: The notebook
steps.quote: He takes one step toward the counter. A voice in his earpiece: one word. He turns and goes.

steps.text: He takes one step toward the counter. A voice in his earpiece: one word. He turns and goes.

steps.title: The blue glow
steps.quote: The door swings shut. The television laughs again.

steps.text: The door swings shut. The television laughs again.
Over black: RAIN.
NOBODY'S WITNESS
MAIN TITLES
THREE DAYS LATER

steps.title: Apartment block
steps.quote: An old four-story apartment block squeezed between newer buildings.

steps.title: Laundry in the rain
steps.quote: Laundry left out on a balcony, getting rained on.

steps.title: The elevated line
steps.quote: A train slides past on the elevated line behind it, windows lit, and the whole building trembles faintly.

steps.text: An old four-story apartment block squeezed between newer buildings. Laundry left out on a balcony, getting rained on. A train slides past on the elevated line behind it, windows lit, and the whole building trembles faintly.

steps.title: The lit window
steps.quote: One window on the third floor is lit.

steps.text: One window on the third floor is lit.

steps.title: The apartment
steps.quote: Small and tidy. Grey light through rain-streaked glass.

steps.text: Small and tidy. Grey light through rain-streaked glass. A smartphone on the table; an old boxy television in the corner. Nothing here quite belongs to one decade.

steps.title: The pale blue umbrella
steps.quote: By the door, in the umbrella stand: a pale blue umbrella. Bone dry.

steps.text: By the door, in the umbrella stand: a pale blue umbrella. Bone dry.

steps.title: The photograph
steps.quote: On a shelf, one framed photograph, its colors gone warm and faded.

steps.text: On a shelf, one framed photograph, its colors gone warm and faded. A Tokyo street, twenty years ago. An American man in a rumpled suit, smiling, holding the hands of two small girls: VERA (9), serious, and MARA (4), mid-laugh. Behind them, the sign of a noodle shop.

steps.title: The room too big
steps.quote: VERA VOSS (29) sits at the low table.

steps.title: Vera at the table
steps.quote: Two cups. Hers holds cold tea. The other is empty and clean, set out as though someone is expected.

steps.title: The empty place
steps.quote: The other is empty and clean, set out as though someone is expected.

steps.text: VERA VOSS (29) sits at the low table. Two cups. Hers holds cold tea. The other is empty and clean, set out as though someone is expected.
Through the thin wall, a neighbour's radio plays an old ballad, muffled: a woman's voice, a song from another decade. Vera doesn't seem to hear it.
Her phone lies face up in front of her. She calls. Waits.

steps.title: The answerphone
steps.quote: It's Mara. You know what to do.

steps.text: It's Mara. You know what to do.
BEEP.

steps.title: Nothing yet
steps.quote: Vera opens her mouth. For a moment, nothing.

steps.text: Vera opens her mouth. For a moment, nothing.

steps.title: The message
steps.quote: You left your umbrella. You'll get soaked.

steps.text: It's me again. I'm not angry anymore. I wasn't really angry then, either. Whatever that man wants, it doesn't matter. I just — You left your umbrella. You'll get soaked. Just call me. You don't have to say anything. Just call, so I know.
She hangs up.

steps.title: At the window
steps.quote: The old television murmurs to itself.

steps.text: The old television murmurs to itself.

...police in Kanda are investigating a double shooting in a small bar in the early hours of Sunday. Two men were killed. Officers say it appears to be a dispute between criminal groups. No arrests have been made...

steps.title: The television
steps.quote: ...rain continuing through the rest of the week...

steps.text: ...rain continuing through the rest of the week...

steps.title: Three looks
steps.quote: She looks at the umbrella by the door. At the clean, empty cup. At the photograph.

steps.text: She looks at the umbrella by the door. At the clean, empty cup. At the photograph.
She stands. Puts on her coat. Hesitates at the door.

steps.title: Takes the umbrella
steps.quote: Then she takes the blue umbrella. Mara's umbrella.

steps.text: Then she takes the blue umbrella. Mara's umbrella.
The door closes behind her. Through the wall, the song on the neighbour's radio ends. A DJ murmurs something. Rain.

scenes.title: The front counter
scenes.heading: INT. POLICE STATION, FRONT COUNTER - NIGHT

steps.title: The front counter
steps.quote: Fluorescent tubes, one of them flickering. A long counter.

steps.text: Fluorescent tubes, one of them flickering. A long counter. Faded posters about pickpockets and traffic safety. An old fax machine beside a new flat monitor. A wall clock that runs a minute fast.

steps.title: Dripping umbrella
steps.quote: Vera stands at the counter, the closed blue umbrella dripping onto the linoleum.

steps.text: Vera stands at the counter, the closed blue umbrella dripping onto the linoleum.

steps.title: The young officer
steps.quote: A YOUNG OFFICER takes her details with polite boredom.

steps.text: A YOUNG OFFICER takes her details with polite boredom. Vera's Japanese is fluent, but careful and slightly formal — learned as a child, relearned as an adult.
Your sister's age?
Twenty-four.
Adults sometimes go away for a few days. Especially foreigners. It's usually —
She doesn't. Not without telling me.

steps.title: Mara voss on screen
steps.quote: He types the name. ON THE MONITOR: MARA VOSS.

steps.text: He types the name. ON THE MONITOR: MARA VOSS.
He stops typing.

steps.title: He stops typing
steps.quote: He looks at the screen a moment too long.

steps.text: He looks at the screen a moment too long. Then he picks up the desk phone and turns away from her.

steps.title: The quiet phone call
steps.quote: Yes. That name. Yes -- the sister is here now.

steps.text: Yes. That name. Yes — the sister is here now.
He hangs up. His manner has changed. Politer.

steps.title: Someone will be right with you
steps.quote: Someone will be right with you.

steps.text: Someone will be right with you.

steps.title: She watches him
steps.quote: Vera looks at him. He doesn't meet her eyes.

steps.text: Vera looks at him. He doesn't meet her eyes.

scenes.title: The interview room
scenes.heading: INT. POLICE STATION, INTERVIEW ROOM - MOMENTS LATER

steps.title: The interview room
steps.quote: Small. A table, two chairs, a box of tissues nobody has touched in years. Rain on a frosted window.

steps.text: Small. A table, two chairs, a box of tissues nobody has touched in years. Rain on a frosted window.

steps.title: The paper cup of tea
steps.quote: DETECTIVE ISHIDA (50s) sets a paper cup of tea in front of Vera. Gentle. Unhurried. Tired, in a way that looks like decency.

steps.text: DETECTIVE ISHIDA (50s) sets a paper cup of tea in front of Vera. Gentle. Unhurried. Tired, in a way that looks like decency.

steps.title: You must be cold
steps.quote: You must be cold.

steps.text: You must be cold.

steps.title: The untouched tea
steps.quote: His English is excellent.

steps.text: His English is excellent.

steps.title: I speak japanese
steps.quote: I speak Japanese.

steps.text: I speak Japanese.
Of course. But this is a difficult thing. It is easier in your own language.
A small beat. She lets it go. For now.
The officer made a phone call the moment he had my sister's name. Then you came.
A foreign passport. We like to take care with these things.

steps.title: The form
steps.quote: He slides a form across the table, and a pen. MISSING PERSON, in Japanese, with an English line beneath.

steps.text: He slides a form across the table, and a pen. MISSING PERSON, in Japanese, with an English line beneath.
Name. Height. What she was wearing, if you know.

steps.title: Her handwriting
steps.quote: She fills it in. Her handwriting is fast and square. Ishida reads it upside down as she writes, without seeming to.

steps.text: She fills it in. Her handwriting is fast and square. Ishida reads it upside down as she writes, without seeming to.
Voss. You grew up here?
Until I was nine.
And your parents? They are in America?
My mother is. My father died.
Here?
Here. When I was a child.
I'm sorry. Did your sister ever talk about him?

steps.title: The pen stops
steps.quote: The pen stops.

steps.text: The pen stops.
She was four. She doesn't remember him.
It is not quite an answer. Ishida lets it be one.
A recent photograph?

steps.title: The passport photo
steps.quote: From behind her card, a small square passport photo: MARA, unsmiling for once, a strand of hair across her eyes.

steps.text: Vera takes her wallet from her bag. From behind her card, a small square passport photo: MARA, unsmiling for once, a strand of hair across her eyes.
She gave me two when she renewed. In case.
In case.

steps.title: Squared to the corner
steps.quote: He takes it by the edges. Looks at it a moment. Sets it on the form, squares it to the corner.

steps.text: He takes it by the edges. Looks at it a moment. Sets it on the form, squares it to the corner.
When did you last see her?

steps.title: Three days ago
steps.quote: Thursday. At my apartment. We had dinner.

steps.text: Thursday. At my apartment. We had dinner.
And how did she seem?
Vera hesitates.
Normal.

steps.title: He waits
steps.quote: Ishida waits, kindly, as if he knows there is more. She doesn't give it.

steps.text: Ishida waits, kindly, as if he knows there is more. She doesn't give it.
Did she ever speak of your family? Anything she had been thinking about?
No.
Did she mention Kanda? Friends there? Work?

steps.title: Why kanda
steps.quote: Kanda? No. Why --

steps.text: Kanda? No. Why —
She stops. Something arrives in her face.
The shootings. In Kanda. It was on the news.
Ishida says nothing. That is its own answer.
Is she hurt?
We have no reason to believe she is hurt.
That's not the same as saying she isn't.
Miss Voss —

steps.title: Is she dead
steps.quote: Is she dead?

steps.text: Is she dead?
We have no reason to believe so.
She hears it: the careful, official shape of the sentence. Her hand tightens around the paper cup.
Stop saying that. Stop saying what you have no reason to believe and tell me what you know.

steps.title: The crushed cup
steps.quote: Hot tea runs over her fingers and onto the table, across the corner of the form.

steps.text: The cup crumples in her fist. Hot tea runs over her fingers and onto the table, across the corner of the form. She doesn't seem to feel it.

steps.title: A matter between criminal groups
steps.quote: What I know is that two men were killed in Kanda, and that it is a matter between criminal groups.

steps.text: What I know is that two men were killed in Kanda, and that it is a matter between criminal groups. And that your sister is a young woman who has not called her sister for three days. Those may be two separate things.
May be.
May be.
Ishida takes a tissue from the box, the first in years, and offers it. She doesn't take it. He sets it down beside her hand.
When she speaks again, it's in Japanese. Low. Precise. Every word placed.

steps.title: In japanese
steps.quote: She is my sister. I have been calling her for days. If you know where she is, tell me.

steps.text: She is my sister. I have been calling her for days. If you know where she is, tell me.
Ishida looks at her a long moment. When he answers, it is in Japanese too, for the first time. Formal. A door closing.

I do not know where she is. That is the truth. And if, on the off chance, she did see something she should not have, then the safest place for her is wherever she is now. And the safest thing you can do is nothing.

steps.title: Rain on the frosted window
steps.quote: Silence. Rain on the frosted window.

steps.text: Silence. Rain on the frosted window.
He switches back to English, gentle again, as if the last minute didn't happen.
Go home, Miss Voss. Keep your phone on. If she calls, call me first. Any hour.

steps.title: The card
steps.quote: He slides his card across the wet table. She looks at it. Then takes it. Stands. Picks up the blue umbrella.

steps.text: He slides his card across the wet table. She looks at it. Then takes it. Stands. Picks up the blue umbrella.
At the door:
You would have told me if she was dead. Wouldn't you?
Of course, I'm sure we will find her, you have my word.
She looks at him. She can't tell. She goes. The door closes behind her.

steps.title: No trace
steps.quote: He wipes the spilled tea from the table with the tissue, slowly, carefully, until there is no trace of it.

steps.text: Ishida sits alone a moment. He wipes the spilled tea from the table with the tissue, slowly, carefully, until there is no trace of it.

steps.title: The inside pocket
steps.quote: Then he picks up the passport photo, dry at the edges, looks at Mara's face, and slides it into his inside pocket. The form he leaves where it is.

steps.text: Then he picks up the passport photo, dry at the edges, looks at Mara's face, and slides it into his inside pocket. The form he leaves where it is.

scenes.title: The detectives' room
scenes.heading: INT. POLICE STATION, DETECTIVES' ROOM - CONTINUOUS

steps.title: The detectives room
steps.quote: Rows of cluttered desks under humming fluorescent light. Most are empty at this hour. A radio plays low somewhere.

steps.text: Rows of cluttered desks under humming fluorescent light. Most are empty at this hour. A radio plays low somewhere.

steps.title: The bottom drawer
steps.quote: Ishida sits at his desk and opens the bottom drawer.

steps.text: Ishida sits at his desk and opens the bottom drawer. The two drawers above it stay closed.
THE DRAWER

steps.title: The evidence bag
steps.quote: Inside the drawer, sealed together in one clear evidence bag: Mara's purse and the torn strap, coiled beside it. Still damp.

steps.text: Inside the drawer, sealed together in one clear evidence bag: Mara's purse and the torn strap, coiled beside it. Still damp.

steps.title: He looks at it
steps.quote: He looks at it a long moment.

steps.title: Drawer closed
steps.quote: Closes the drawer.

steps.text: He looks at it a long moment. Closes the drawer.

steps.title: The clock
steps.quote: On the wall, the clock runs a minute fast.

steps.text: On the wall, the clock runs a minute fast.

steps.title: Were closed
steps.quote: The same bar in flat grey daylight. It looks smaller without the night. Chairs up on the counter. The CRT television is dark.

steps.text: The same bar in flat grey daylight. It looks smaller without the night. Chairs up on the counter. The CRT television is dark.
Where the journalist fell, there is a new rubber floor mat, too clean for this room.
OKADA (60s), the bar's owner, mops around it without looking at it. He has the stillness of a man who hasn't slept.
The door opens. Vera, the blue umbrella in her hand.
We're closed.
Vera holds up her phone: a photo of Mara, laughing at a party, a paper crown on her head.
My sister. Four nights ago. Was she here?

steps.title: Exactly one second
steps.quote: Okada looks at the photo for exactly one second.

steps.text: Okada looks at the photo for exactly one second.
No.
You didn't look.
I looked. No.

steps.title: The far end
steps.quote: His eyes go, just once, to the far end of the counter. Then back to the mop.

steps.text: His eyes go, just once, to the far end of the counter. Then back to the mop.
Vera sees it. She doesn't push. She bows, small and polite, and leaves.

steps.title: The umbrella left behind
steps.quote: She has left the blue umbrella leaning against a stool. Okada looks at the umbrella for a long moment.

steps.text: She has left the blue umbrella leaning against a stool.
Okada looks at the umbrella for a long moment.
Rain. Vera walks away down the narrow street, no umbrella, head down.
Miss.

steps.title: Miss
steps.quote: She turns. Okada stands in the bar doorway holding the blue umbrella, out of breath, as if deciding something cost him more than the walk.

steps.text: She turns. Okada stands in the bar doorway holding the blue umbrella, out of breath, as if deciding something cost him more than the walk.

steps.title: Behind the counter
steps.quote: Then he holds out his other hand. In it: the small red enamel bird clip.

steps.text: He hands it to her. Then he holds out his other hand. In it: the small red enamel bird clip.
Vera stops breathing.

steps.title: It was mine
steps.quote: It was mine. She took it when we were kids. She never gave it back.

steps.text: It was mine. She took it when we were kids. She never gave it back.
She has said it in English, without realizing. Okada doesn't understand the words. He understands her face.
Behind the counter. After.
Did you give this to the police?
They didn't ask.

steps.title: Not the police. Him.
steps.quote: He takes a business card from his apron and presses it into her hand.

steps.text: He takes a business card from his apron and presses it into her hand. Old, soft at the corners, handwritten on the back.
Not the police. Him.
Who is he?
He found my daughter once. When no one else would look.
He goes back inside before she can thank him.

steps.title: The card
steps.quote: Vera looks at the card. Printed in English and in katakana: JACK. INVESTIGATIONS. An address. No surname.

steps.text: Vera looks at the card. Printed in English and in katakana: JACK. INVESTIGATIONS. An address. No surname.

steps.title: Pressed against the railway
steps.quote: Second floor of an old building pressed against the elevated railway.

steps.text: Second floor of an old building pressed against the elevated railway. One room. Frosted glass door, JACK hand-lettered on it in English and in katakana.
A desk. A black rotary phone. Filing cabinets. A small CRT television on the cabinet, muted, playing an old black-and-white samurai film. A sofa that has clearly been slept on.
A TRAIN passes outside. The blinds shiver. A spoon rattles in an empty cup. Then silence again.

steps.title: Open and shut
steps.quote: He flicks an old steel lighter open and shut, open and shut.

steps.text: JACK (48) sits at the desk eating a convenience-store rice ball, watching the silent swordsmen. Handsome once, in a way he stopped maintaining. A good coat, badly kept. He flicks an old steel lighter open and shut, open and shut. There are no cigarettes anywhere.

steps.title: Depends whos calling
steps.quote: A knock on the frosted glass. Vera comes in, wet, the blue umbrella dripping.

steps.text: A knock on the frosted glass. Vera comes in, wet, the blue umbrella dripping.
Are you the one they call Jack?
Depends who's calling.
Mr. Okada. The bar in Kanda.
Jack puts the rice ball down.
Sit down.
She sits. He doesn't switch to English. He lets her speak in the language she chose. She notices.

steps.title: Four days
steps.quote: My sister has been missing for four days. The police say to go home and wait.

steps.text: My sister has been missing for four days. The police say to go home and wait.
I don't do missing persons. People who go missing usually want to.

steps.title: The clip on the desk
steps.quote: She places the red bird clip on his desk.

steps.text: She places the red bird clip on his desk.
She was in that bar. The night two men were shot there.
Jack looks at the clip for a long moment. The lighter stops.
What did the police tell you?
To go home.
It's good advice.
Is it yours, too?
He doesn't answer. Another train passes. The blinds shiver.
Do you have photographs of her?
She takes an envelope from her bag. As she pulls out the photos, something slides out with them and falls face up on the desk:

steps.title: Face up
steps.quote: The old framed photograph from her shelf, taken out of its frame.

steps.text: The old framed photograph from her shelf, taken out of its frame. Twenty years ago. The American man in the rumpled suit. The two small girls. The noodle shop sign behind them.
Jack looks at it.
He does not move. On the TV behind him, a sword is drawn in total silence.
That's us. Before we left.
She has slipped into English. So does he, quietly.
Your father.
He died. That year. Here.

steps.title: By its edges
steps.quote: Jack picks the photograph up by its edges, carefully, the way you'd handle evidence. Or something fragile.

steps.text: Jack picks the photograph up by its edges, carefully, the way you'd handle evidence. Or something fragile. He looks a moment too long at the noodle shop sign. Then he sets it down, face up, and squares it to the edge of the desk.
I'm sorry.
It was a long time ago.
Yes.
A beat.
Ten thousand yen a day. Plus expenses. I'll need a key to her apartment, her phone number, her friends, where she worked, where she drank.

steps.title: So you'll look
steps.quote: So you'll look.

steps.text: So you'll look.
I'll look.
She gathers the photographs, and the red bird clip with them. He watches it go back into her pocket. He doesn't ask for it.
At the door, she stops.

steps.title: At the door
steps.quote: Mr. Okada said you found his daughter.

steps.text: Mr. Okada said you found his daughter.
I found her.
Was she alive?
Jack looks at her. The honest answer is in the pause.
Her Japanese. Your sister's. Is it good?
Some. Badly.
Then she stands out. That helps.

steps.title: Down the stairs
steps.quote: Through the frosted glass, her shape goes down the stairs and is gone.

steps.text: Vera nods. Goes. Through the frosted glass, her shape goes down the stairs and is gone.
Jack sits very still.
Past midnight. Only the desk lamp and the grey flicker of the television, now showing static.

steps.title: The box
steps.quote: Jack crouches at the grey steel cupboard under the window, pulls its door open and takes out a cardboard box he has kept behind the files. Dust on the lid. He hasn't opened it in years.

steps.text: Jack crouches at the grey steel cupboard under the window, pulls its door open and takes out a cardboard box he has kept behind the files. Dust on the lid. He hasn't opened it in years.
Inside: a police notebook. An old ID card with a younger face. A folded newspaper clipping.
THE CLIPPING

steps.title: Daniel voss 41
steps.quote: An English-language newspaper, yellowed. A small headline: AMERICAN INSURANCE INVESTIGATOR FOUND DEAD - POLICE RULE SUICIDE. A photograph: the same man from Vera's picture. The caption: DANIEL VOSS, 41.

steps.text: An English-language newspaper, yellowed. A small headline: AMERICAN INSURANCE INVESTIGATOR FOUND DEAD - POLICE RULE SUICIDE. A photograph: the same man from Vera's picture. The caption: DANIEL VOSS, 41.

steps.title: Two men laughing
steps.quote: Beneath the clipping, one more photograph. Two men at a tiny noodle counter, laughing, steam in the air: DANIEL VOSS, and a much younger JACK, still in a cheap police-issue suit.

steps.text: Beneath the clipping, one more photograph. Two men at a tiny noodle counter, laughing, steam in the air: DANIEL VOSS, and a much younger JACK, still in a cheap police-issue suit.
Behind them, the same noodle shop sign.
Jack looks at it for a long time.

steps.title: It takes a long time to dial
steps.quote: Then he dials the rotary phone. It takes a long time to dial.

steps.text: Then he dials the rotary phone. It takes a long time to dial.
It's late, Jack.
The Voss girl came to see me.
I know.
Silence on the line. Rain on the window.
Her sister was in that bar.
The sister is a missing persons case. The bar is a gang matter. Two separate things.
And the old man in the street?
Sakai. Yes. That Sakai. I know what you're thinking. Old debts, old enemies. It's a gang matter.

steps.title: Twenty years
steps.quote: Twenty years, Ishida.

steps.text: Twenty years, Ishida.
A long pause.
Go to sleep, Jack. You found enough twenty years ago. You're too old to be haunted.

steps.title: The line
steps.quote: The line goes dead. Jack holds the receiver a moment longer.

steps.text: The line goes dead.

steps.title: He sets the receiver down
steps.quote: Jack holds the receiver a moment longer. He sets it down.

steps.title: The lighter
steps.quote: He sets it down. Flicks the lighter open. Shut.

steps.text: Jack holds the receiver a moment longer. He sets it down. Flicks the lighter open. Shut.
A train passes. The photograph of the two laughing men trembles on the desk.
The street from the cold open. The rain hasn't stopped in four days.

steps.title: Not searching, looking
steps.quote: Jack walks it slowly, a cheap clear plastic umbrella over his head.

steps.text: Jack walks it slowly, a cheap clear plastic umbrella over his head. Not searching. Looking.
The vending machine at the corner. He feeds it a coin. A can of hot coffee drops.
Thank you very much.
He holds the can without drinking it and looks at the spot where Sakai died. Nothing there now. Rain on asphalt.
He turns and looks at the barbershop doorway. Steps into it. Stands exactly where Mara stood.
From here, he can see the whole street. And, at the far end, the small lit sign of Okada's bar.
He looks at the barbershop pole beside him. Crouches.

steps.title: The strap
steps.quote: Caught on a rough metal edge at knee height: a short twist of torn leather strap.

steps.text: Caught on a rough metal edge at knee height: a short twist of torn leather strap.
He doesn't touch it. He looks from the strap, to the spot where Sakai fell, to the bar sign. Reconstructing it.

steps.title: The barber
steps.quote: A shutter RATTLES up above him. A BARBER (80s), in pajamas, looks down from the upstairs window.

steps.text: A shutter RATTLES up above him. A BARBER (80s), in pajamas, looks down from the upstairs window.
Police again?
Not for a long time.
The barber considers him.
I told them. I was asleep. I heard the shot. Then a car.
One car?

steps.title: One car, twice
steps.quote: One car. Twice.

steps.text: One car. Twice. It left. Then it came back.
Jack looks down the empty street.
Why come back?

steps.title: Everywhere a small thing could fall
steps.quote: He looks down the street at the drains, the doorways, the gutter: everywhere a small thing could fall.

steps.text: Nobody answers. He looks down the street at the drains, the doorways, the gutter: everywhere a small thing could fall.
The barber shrugs and pulls the shutter down.
He looks again at the doorway. At the bar sign. At the torn strap.
She was here. She saw it. She ran there. She saw that too.
And whatever they came back for, she has it.
He looks down the empty street at the bar sign. And one more question he can't answer yet: what was an American girl doing in a Kanda backstreet at one in the morning?

steps.title: The can
steps.quote: Jack drops the unopened coffee into the recycling bin. The can CLANKS. The crossing melody starts up somewhere, for no one.

steps.text: Jack drops the unopened coffee into the recycling bin. The can CLANKS. The crossing melody starts up somewhere, for no one.

scenes.title: Someone who meant to come back
scenes.heading: INT. MARA'S APARTMENT - DAY

steps.text: A tiny studio in an old building. Grey daylight. Clothes on every surface. Sketches taped to the walls: pencil, charcoal, cheap watercolour. Trains. Rooftops. Laundry lines. Faces on the subway.
The room smells of someone who meant to come back.

steps.title: Someone who meant to come back
steps.quote: Vera stands just inside the door. She hasn't taken her coat off. Jack moves through the room slowly, touching nothing yet. Looking.

steps.text: Vera stands just inside the door. She hasn't taken her coat off. Jack moves through the room slowly, touching nothing yet. Looking.
When were you last here?
A week ago. She made me coffee. It was terrible.

steps.title: The fridge
steps.quote: Jack opens the fridge. Milk. A half-eaten cake in a box.

steps.text: Jack opens the fridge. Milk. A half-eaten cake in a box. He closes it.
She wasn't planning to disappear.
No.

steps.title: Packed and zipped
steps.quote: He crouches by the futon. A suitcase underneath, packed and zipped.

steps.text: He crouches by the futon. A suitcase underneath, packed and zipped. He looks at it, then at Vera.
That was for America. She'd booked a flight. Next month.
You didn't want her to go.
I didn't want her to run away again. That's what I said. The night she left. That she always runs.

steps.title: The wall of drawings
steps.quote: She looks at the wall of drawings, not at him.

steps.text: She looks at the wall of drawings, not at him.

steps.title: It's always about Dad
steps.quote: It was about Dad. It's always about Dad.

steps.text: It was about Dad. It's always about Dad. She wanted to dig it all up. Who he was here. Why he — I told her to leave him dead. She said I was the one who ran. All the way back here, chasing a ghost, and I won't even look at it. I told her to go, then. Go home. Those were the last things I said to her.
Jack says nothing. He knows better than to comfort it away.
On the desk: a thick sketchbook, its cover soft with use. Jack opens it.

steps.title: The sketchbook
steps.quote: Page after page of the same place. A tiny noodle counter under a railway. Six stools. A curtain. A hand-painted sign.

steps.text: Page after page of the same place. A tiny noodle counter under a railway. Six stools. A curtain. A hand-painted sign. Drawn over and over, from different angles, in different years of her hand — a child's crayon version taped inside the cover, the newest in careful ink.
She drew this a lot.
Vera glances over.

steps.title: A story I used to tell her
steps.quote: Since she was little.

steps.text: Since she was little. It's from a story I used to tell her. About the noodle shop Dad took us to. She was too young to remember it, so I told her. She made it up from what I said. It's not real.

steps.title: Every stroke correct
steps.quote: Jack turns a page. The sign, in careful ink. Every stroke of the kanji correct.

steps.text: Jack turns a page. The sign, in careful ink. Every stroke of the kanji correct.
He has seen this sign. Twice this week. Once in the photograph from Vera's shelf, on his own desk. Once in a box in his own cupboard.
Can I borrow this?
Why?
Jack doesn't answer. He looks at the drawing a moment too long.

steps.title: The clip on the sketchbook
steps.quote: Vera takes the hair clip out of her coat pocket and sets it on the sketchbook.

steps.text: Vera takes the hair clip out of her coat pocket and sets it on the sketchbook.
Take this too. It's mine. She stole it.
He takes both.
She hesitates, then nods. He closes the sketchbook and puts it under his arm, and says nothing else about it.

steps.title: The mirror
steps.quote: From the rear-view mirror, on a loop of string, the red bird clip swings with each turn.

steps.text: Rain. Wipers. Kanda's wet streets slide past the windscreen. From the rear-view mirror, on a loop of string, the red bird clip swings with each turn.
In the mirror, behind it: a pair of headlights. The same distance, every turn. Never closer, never farther.
Jack watches them. One hand goes into his coat pocket and closes around the lighter. He takes a corner a shade too fast, then slow. The headlights follow, dipped, patient.

steps.title: The lane mouth
steps.quote: He stops at the mouth of the lane, exactly where the sedan stopped, and kills the engine and lights.

steps.text: He stops at the mouth of the lane, exactly where the sedan stopped, and kills the engine and lights.
Forty metres back, the headlights slow. Stop. Go out.
He waits, long enough to be sure. Then he gets out and walks back along the wet road toward the dark car, one hand in his pocket.
A small, boxy, maroon hatchback, its glass steamed. He raps on the driver's window with a knuckle.
It winds down. Vera, both hands on the wheel.

steps.title: The lighter
steps.quote: He takes his hand from his pocket. The old steel lighter, open, unlit.

steps.text: He takes his hand from his pocket. The old steel lighter, open, unlit.
Is that what you were holding?
It's what I had.
He snaps it shut.

steps.title: Forty metres
steps.quote: Forty metres. Twenty minutes. You never once lost me.

steps.text: Forty metres. Twenty minutes. You never once lost me.
Is that bad?
It's what a professional does.
Who did you think I was?
Somebody who'd be worse company.
You said you'd look. You didn't say where. I waited outside your office.
If you can follow me, so can they.

steps.title: She hadn't thought of that
steps.quote: She hadn't thought of that. She looks past him at the empty road.

steps.text: She hadn't thought of that. She looks past him at the empty road.
I brought food.
He sighs the sigh of a man who has lost an argument he was never allowed to make.
Park round the corner, then get in mine. One car is a man waiting. Two is somebody watching.

steps.title: Engine off
steps.quote: Engine off. Rain on the windscreen, no wipers; the glass turns the lane into smears of light.

steps.text: LATER. Engine off. Rain on the windscreen, no wipers; the glass turns the lane into smears of light. At the far end, small and amber, the bar sign.
Vera shakes the blue umbrella out onto his floor. From a paper bag, two convenience-store rice balls. She holds one out.
You were eating one when I came in. I assumed it was a lifestyle.
This is a stakeout. Nothing happens.
Then I won't miss anything.

steps.title: Their fingers don't touch
steps.quote: He takes it. Their fingers don't touch.

steps.text: He takes it. Their fingers don't touch. Both notice that they don't.
They watch the lane.
What are we waiting for?
Whoever comes back.
Back?
Someone came back to this street that night. Nobody comes back for what they already have.
What didn't they have?
I don't know yet.

steps.title: The red bird swings
steps.quote: The mirror trembles, and the red bird swings.

steps.text: A TRAIN passes somewhere behind them. The mirror trembles, and the red bird swings. Vera watches it.
Is that for luck?
It's so I don't lose it.

steps.title: The rice ball
steps.quote: A long silence. The rice ball in her lap, unwrapped, uneaten.

steps.text: A long silence. The rice ball in her lap, unwrapped, uneaten.
I told her she always runs.
You said.
It's the last thing I —

steps.title: Not running from you
steps.quote: Whatever happened to her, she wasn't running from you.

steps.text: Runners don't pack. They leave with what they're wearing. Your sister had a suitcase zipped under the bed and a flight booked home. Whatever happened to her, she wasn't running from you.
You don't know that.
No. But I'd bet on it.
She looks at him for the first time since she sat down. He is looking at the lane. He doesn't look back.

steps.title: A figure at the road end
steps.quote: A figure at the road end, under a black umbrella tilted low, face lost beneath it.

steps.text: A figure at the road end, under a black umbrella tilted low, face lost beneath it. He walks past the car (both of them sink an inch in their seats) and into the lane.

steps.title: The shuttered door
steps.quote: He goes to the bar's shuttered door. Tries the handle. Stands under the amber sign, looking up and down the lane.

steps.text: He goes to the bar's shuttered door. Tries the handle. Stands under the amber sign, looking up and down the lane. Then he turns back toward the road, and the umbrella swings toward the car.

steps.title: Reflex
steps.quote: Jack's arm goes out across Vera, pressing her back into the seat. Not looking. Reflex.

steps.text: Jack's arm goes out across Vera, pressing her back into the seat. Not looking. Reflex.
The umbrella holds on them. Then turns away. The man walks to a small white car further up the road, and gets in. He doesn't start it. He sits.
Jack looks at his own arm, still across her chest, as if it belonged to someone else. He takes it back.

steps.title: The plate
steps.quote: Jack finds a pencil stub, smooths the paper bag flat on his knee, and writes the plate number on it.

steps.text: They sit very still. After a long time, the white car pulls out and goes, without hurry. Jack finds a pencil stub, smooths the paper bag flat on his knee, and writes the plate number on it.
Is that routine? Watching a bar after a shooting?
Probably.
He folds the bag once and puts it inside his coat.
You don't think so.
I think it's a plate number.

steps.title: The amber sign goes dark
steps.quote: 3:40 a.m. The amber sign at the far end goes dark.

steps.text: 3:40 a.m. The amber sign at the far end goes dark. Jack starts the engine.
Call me when you go somewhere.
I will.
That's a lie.
Yes.
She sets the rice ball on his dashboard, still untouched, and gets out.

steps.title: The dark takes it
steps.quote: In the mirror he watches the blue umbrella go up the wet road and round the corner, and the dark take it.

steps.text: In the mirror he watches the blue umbrella go up the wet road and round the corner, and the dark take it.

steps.title: Forty metres back
steps.quote: Jack counts ten. Then he pulls out after them, forty metres back. Never closer. Never farther.

steps.text: A small engine starts, out of sight. Headlights swing across the end of the road and away. Jack counts ten. Then he pulls out after them, forty metres back. Never closer. Never farther.
Rain. A wide street of new glass towers and chain stores.

steps.title: A gap in someones teeth
steps.quote: Behind it, low and dark and patched, the Hive.

steps.text: Between two towers, a long white construction hoarding: KUROSE DEVELOPMENT, and a painted plaza full of smiling people who don't exist. Behind it, low and dark and patched, the Hive.

steps.title: The Hive
steps.quote: A dense, self-built block of stacked homes and workshops rising eleven storeys

steps.text: A dense, self-built block of stacked homes and workshops rising eleven storeys, balconies bolted onto balconies, air conditioners and pipes and laundry and hand-painted signs, all of it crushed together under the curve of the elevated railway. The city has grown up around it and forgotten it is there.

At the back, the tower steps down to a low rear wing pressed hard against the concrete railway viaduct, its roof level with the tracks. Old neon signs hang dead on its face. Even in daylight the Hive sits in its own haze of steam and kitchen smoke, as if it had its own weather.
Jack stands on the pavement with the sketchbook under his coat. He looks up at the Hive for a long moment, as if at someone he used to know.

steps.title: Then he goes in
steps.quote: Then he goes in.

steps.text: Then he goes in.

steps.title: Barely shoulder-wide
steps.quote: Narrow corridors, barely shoulder-wide, lit by bare bulbs.

steps.text: Narrow corridors, barely shoulder-wide, lit by bare bulbs. Water drips from somewhere above and runs along the floor in a thin shining line. Pipes overhead. Wires everywhere. What daylight gets in comes in thin cold shafts from gaps far overhead, thick with drifting steam.

steps.title: The chair
steps.quote: A dentist's chair behind a curtain, a hand-lettered price list taped to the wall.

steps.text: Doors stand open onto other lives. A MAN at a bench mending radios, a dozen of them murmuring different stations at once. A FAMILY eating dinner at four in the afternoon, the TV loud. An OLD WOMAN asleep in front of a sumo match. A dentist's chair behind a curtain, a hand-lettered price list taped to the wall.

steps.title: Everybody sees him
steps.quote: Jack walks through it all. Nobody stops him. Everybody sees him.

steps.text: Jack walks through it all. Nobody stops him. Everybody sees him.
A TRAIN passes overhead. The whole building trembles. Dust sifts down through the bulb light. Nobody looks up.
He turns a corner and stops.
The noodle counter. Six stools. The curtain. The hand-painted sign, faded almost to nothing but unmistakable.

steps.title: Exactly the drawing
steps.quote: It is exactly the drawing.

steps.text: It is exactly the drawing.
Steam. A single fluorescent tube. Two customers slurping in silence at the far end.
Behind the counter, KANEKO (70s), tiny and sharp-eyed, works a pot with long chopsticks. She looks up as Jack sits at the counter.

steps.title: You got old
steps.quote: She looks at him for a long time. Longer than a stranger would.

steps.text: She looks at him for a long time. Longer than a stranger would.
You got old.
So did you.

steps.title: I was already old
steps.quote: I was already old.

steps.text: I was already old. You were a boy in a cheap suit, the only foreign face on the force. Japanese papers, American face. You came here with the American. Everything is going. We are just slower.

steps.title: The empty third stool
steps.quote: Jack looks at the counter under his hands.

steps.text: Jack looks at the counter under his hands.
I'm looking for his daughter. The younger one.
Kaneko's chopsticks don't pause.
The little one? She was four years old. She ate rice with her fingers.
She's twenty-four now. And someone wants to kill her.
The two customers at the end of the counter have stopped slurping.

steps.title: Eat then go
steps.quote: Kaneko sets a bowl of noodles in front of Jack.

steps.text: Kaneko sets a bowl of noodles in front of Jack.
Eat. Then go. There is no one here but us.
Jack eats. Slowly. He finishes everything.

steps.title: More than the bowl costs
steps.quote: He puts down more money than the bowl costs, far more, and a business card on top of it.

steps.text: He puts down more money than the bowl costs, far more, and a business card on top of it.
He always paid too much, too.
He goes. Kaneko looks at the card for a long moment.

steps.title: Something moves
steps.quote: Behind the curtain, in the dark of the storeroom, something moves.

steps.text: Behind the curtain, in the dark of the storeroom, something moves.

steps.title: The last page
steps.quote: Jack sits in the dark, the sketchbook open on the desk.

steps.text: Rain. The old television plays static. Jack sits in the dark, the sketchbook open on the desk.
He turns to the last page. Tucked inside the back cover: a letter, folded small, creased as though it had been crumpled into a ball and smoothed flat again.
He unfolds it under the lamp. Cheap lined paper. Careful, laborious English handwriting.
THE LETTER

"Miss Voss. Your father did not kill himself. I can prove it. I have kept his papers for twenty years. I am old and I am ill and I do not want to carry them any more. Please telephone." A phone number. The signature: T. SAKAI.

steps.title: The letter
steps.quote: The envelope folded inside it is addressed to VERA VOSS.

steps.text: The envelope folded inside it is addressed to VERA VOSS.
Jack reads the letter twice. Then he looks at the name on the envelope for a long time.
The black rotary phone RINGS.
He answers. Listens.

steps.title: After the last train
steps.quote: Come back. Alone. After the last train.

steps.text: Come back. Alone. After the last train.
The line clicks dead.
Past midnight. The shutter half down. The fluorescent tube is off; only a single bulb burns.

steps.title: She stands aside
steps.quote: Kaneko lifts the curtain to the storeroom and stands aside.

steps.text: Kaneko lifts the curtain to the storeroom and stands aside.

scenes.title: Prove it
scenes.heading: INT. THE HIVE, NOODLE SHOP STOREROOM - CONTINUOUS

steps.text: Flour sacks. The futon. The bare bulb.
MARA sits on the futon with her knees up and her phone to her ear, listening.
You left your umbrella. You'll get soaked. Just call me. You don't have to say anything. Just call, so I know.

steps.title: The voicemail
steps.quote: The message ends. She plays it again.

steps.text: The message ends. She plays it again.

steps.title: Prove it
steps.quote: Jack is in the doorway. She scrambles back against the wall.

steps.text: Jack is in the doorway. She scrambles back against the wall.
My name is Jack. Your sister hired me.
Prove it.

steps.title: The red bird clip
steps.quote: Jack sets her sketchbook on a flour sack between them, with the hair clip on top.

steps.text: Jack sets her sketchbook on a flour sack between them, with the hair clip on top.
Mara stares at it.
She says it was hers. She says you stole it when you were kids and never gave it back.
Something in Mara's face gives way.
It was never hers. Dad gave it to me. She just says that.

steps.title: The book into her lap
steps.quote: She pulls the sketchbook into her lap.

steps.title: The clip on the book
steps.quote: She pulls the sketchbook into her lap.

steps.text: She pulls the sketchbook into her lap.
She almost laughs, and then she is crying, silently, pressing the back of her wrist against her mouth.

steps.title: He makes himself smaller
steps.quote: Jack waits. He doesn't go to her. He sits down on a flour sack, slowly, making himself smaller.

steps.text: Jack waits. He doesn't go to her. He sits down on a flour sack, slowly, making himself smaller.
Is she okay? Is she — does she know you're —
He doesn't answer. So she asks again.
Is she okay?
She's been calling you. She hasn't slept.
I know. I listen to them.
Why were you in Kanda, Mara?
She looks at him. Decides.

steps.title: He wrote to Vera
steps.quote: He wrote to Vera. Mr. Sakai.

steps.text: He wrote to Vera. Mr. Sakai. She threw it in the bin without even answering. I took it out. I called him. He said he had Dad's papers. He said to come to the bar at one o'clock. There'd be a man from a newspaper there too, so it couldn't be buried again. I sent them both a photo so they'd know me. He wrote back one line. "You have his face."

steps.title: Vera doesn't know
steps.quote: Vera doesn't know you went.

steps.text: Vera doesn't know you went.

steps.title: I called her a coward
steps.quote: I called her a coward. (small, bitter laugh) And I'm the one hiding in a storeroom.

steps.title: The coward line
steps.quote: I called her a coward. (small, bitter laugh) And I'm the one hiding in a storeroom.

steps.text: We had a fight about it. I called her a coward. And I'm the one hiding in a storeroom. Don't tell her I'm here.
She's your sister.

They have my purse. My passport. They know my name. They know where I live, where she lives, all of it. If she knows where I am, she'll come here. She won't be able to help it. And they'll follow her. They'll use her to get to me. And then they'll kill her too.
You don't know that.
I watched them shoot two men like they were switching off lights.

steps.title: The bulb hums
steps.quote: Silence. The bulb hums.

steps.text: Silence. The bulb hums.
Promise me.
Jack looks at her for a long moment. Twenty years of silence sit behind his eyes.
I promise.
Grey light. Rain on the window. Jack hasn't slept. He is in yesterday's shirt.

steps.title: Footsteps on the stairs
steps.quote: Footsteps on the stairs. The frosted glass. Vera's shape.

steps.text: Footsteps on the stairs. The frosted glass. Vera's shape.
She comes in carrying two coffees in paper cups. She puts one on his desk.
You look terrible.
Thank you.
She sits. She doesn't take her coat off. She waits.
Did you find anything?

steps.title: Not yet
steps.quote: The sketchbook is on the desk between them. Jack's hand rests on its cover.

steps.text: The sketchbook is on the desk between them. Jack's hand rests on its cover.
A train passes. The blinds shiver.
Not yet.
She nods. Believes him. That's the worst part.
Okay. Okay. Tomorrow, then.
She stands. At the door she hesitates, as though she wants to say something else. She doesn't. She goes.

steps.title: He holds it without drinking
steps.quote: He picks up the coffee she brought him and holds it without drinking, the way he held the can at the vending machine.

steps.text: Jack sits very still. He picks up the coffee she brought him and holds it without drinking, the way he held the can at the vending machine.

scenes.title: Somewhere like this
scenes.heading: INT. ALL-NIGHT NOODLE COUNTER, UNDER THE TRACKS - NIGHT
scenes.place: ALL-NIGHT NOODLE COUNTER, UNDER THE TRACKS

steps.title: Somewhere like this
steps.quote: A different place: a narrow standing-and-stools counter wedged into a brick railway arch.

steps.text: A different place: a narrow standing-and-stools counter wedged into a brick railway arch. A ticket machine by the door. Yellowed menus on the wall. A radio behind the counter plays baseball, low.
11:40 p.m. by the clock over the door.
Vera and Jack sit side by side at the counter. Empty bowls. Two coffees in thick white cups. They have been here a long time.

steps.title: The cups tremble
steps.quote: Every few minutes, a train rumbles overhead, and the cups tremble in their saucers.

steps.text: Every few minutes, a train rumbles overhead, and the cups tremble in their saucers.
He used to bring us somewhere like this. Dad. After work. Mara would fall asleep on the counter and he'd carry her home.
And you?

steps.title: I stayed awake
steps.quote: I stayed awake.

steps.text: I stayed awake. I wanted to hear everything he said to the man who made the noodles. I didn't understand any of it. I just liked that he was different here. Lighter. I think he was happy here. Before.
Jack looks down at his cup.

steps.title: Under the arch
steps.quote: They said he killed himself.

steps.text: They said he killed himself. My mother never talked about it. Not once. We went home and it was as if Tokyo never happened.
Do you believe it?

steps.title: A long time
steps.quote: She thinks about it for a long time.

steps.text: She thinks about it for a long time.
I believe he was sad. I don't know if I believe the rest. A man wrote to me last week. He said Dad didn't do it. He said the police knew.
Jack keeps his eyes on his bowl.
What did you do?
I threw it in the bin. Because if it's true, then someone did it. And nobody looked. Twenty years, and nobody even looked.

steps.title: The inside pocket
steps.quote: Jack is very still. The letter is in the inside pocket of his coat. He doesn't move to touch it.

steps.text: Jack is very still. The letter is in the inside pocket of his coat. He doesn't move to touch it.
A train. The cups tremble.

steps.title: Easy to talk to
steps.quote: You're very easy to talk to. It's annoying.

steps.text: You're very easy to talk to. It's annoying.

steps.title: Paid to listen
steps.quote: I get paid to listen.

steps.text: I get paid to listen.
You're not getting paid right now.
He has no answer to that.

steps.title: She rests her head
steps.quote: She rests her head on her folded arms on the counter.

steps.text: She rests her head on her folded arms on the counter. Just for a moment. Her eyes close.
You're the first person I've trusted since she disappeared. Did you know that?
Jack looks at her. His mouth opens. The truth is right there.
Vera —
But she is asleep.
He sits and watches her breathe. A train passes. Her coffee cup, near her elbow, trembles toward the edge of the counter.

steps.title: Back from the edge
steps.quote: He reaches over and moves it back from the edge. Carefully. Quietly. So it won't wake her.

steps.text: He reaches over and moves it back from the edge. Carefully. Quietly. So it won't wake her.
He doesn't wake her. He sits there until the counterman begins stacking chairs.

scenes.title: You never call
scenes.heading: EXT. YAKITORI STALL, UNDER THE TRACKS - NIGHT

steps.text: Smoke. Red paper lanterns. Salarymen at plastic tables under a railway bridge, talking too loud.
Ishida sits alone at a corner table with a beer and a plate of skewers. Jack sits down opposite him.

steps.title: You never call
steps.quote: You never call me unless you want something.

steps.text: You never call me unless you want something.
Sakai.

steps.title: The skewer turns
steps.quote: Ishida sighs. Turns a skewer over with his chopsticks.

steps.text: Ishida sighs. Turns a skewer over with his chopsticks.

steps.title: In the bubble years
steps.quote: You already know what he was. In the bubble years he cleared land.

steps.text: You already know what he was. In the bubble years he cleared land. Old tenants who wouldn't sell. First he'd bring flowers. Then he'd bring men. Then something would happen. A fire, sometimes.

steps.title: The Shiohama fire
steps.quote: The Shiohama fire.

steps.text: The Shiohama fire.

Among others. The journalist in the bar was from the Toto Shimbun. He'd been asking about the redevelopment money. Who owns what. Whose friends vote on what. The usual. Sakai called him a week ago. We think Sakai wanted to confess something before he died. He had cancer. Months left.
Confess what?
Who knows. An old man's conscience. It's very common.

steps.title: Jack watches him
steps.quote: Jack watches him.

steps.text: Jack watches him.
Why are you telling me all this?

steps.title: He puts down his chopsticks
steps.quote: Ishida puts down his chopsticks.

steps.text: Ishida puts down his chopsticks.

Because you'll find out anyway. And because I would rather you heard it from me than from someone who wants to hurt you. Twenty years ago I told you to sign that report. You were young. You did what your senior told you. That was on me, not on you.
I still signed it.

steps.title: Carried it too
steps.quote: And I've carried it too. Every day.

steps.text: And I've carried it too. Every day. Whatever Sakai hid, Jack, if you find it, bring it to me. Not to the department. To me. I'll know what to do with it this time.
Sakai had a wife.
Separated. A fishing town on the Boso coast. The police have spoken to her. She gave us nothing.

steps.title: The address
steps.quote: He takes a napkin, writes an address on it in careful longhand, and slides it across the table. Nothing in his face at all.

steps.text: He takes a napkin, writes an address on it in careful longhand, and slides it across the table. Nothing in his face at all.

steps.title: The lanterns sway
steps.quote: A train roars overhead. The lanterns sway.

steps.text: A long pause. A train roars overhead. The lanterns sway.

steps.title: Jack nods slowly
steps.quote: Jack nods slowly.

steps.text: Jack nods slowly.
It is exactly what he needed to hear. That is what makes it dangerous.

scenes.title: The number 114
scenes.heading: INT. THE HIVE, NOODLE SHOP STOREROOM - NIGHT

steps.title: The number 114
steps.quote: The bulb. The flour sacks. Mara sits cross-legged on the futon.

steps.text: The bulb. The flour sacks. Mara sits cross-legged on the futon. Jack sits against the opposite wall.

steps.title: Eat
steps.quote: Kaneko brings in a bowl of rice, steam rising into the bulb light.

steps.text: The curtain moves. Kaneko brings in a bowl of rice, steam rising into the bulb light.
Eat.
Thank you. Has anyone... come? Asking?
Nobody comes here who isn't lost.
She puts the bowl in Mara's hands. The curtain falls shut behind her.
The rice goes cold in Mara's lap. They talk quietly, as if the building is listening. It is.
Mr. Sakai said "twenty years." Before they shot him. Like he'd been expecting them for twenty years.
He probably had.

steps.title: He knew me
steps.quote: He knew me.

steps.text: He knew me. He saw me in the doorway and stopped. And at the end he pressed the key into my hand. "Don't let them have it."
Jack looks down at his hands.

steps.title: The drawing
steps.quote: Beside the futon, held down by a flour scoop: a stack of loose pages covered in pencil.

steps.text: Beside the futon, held down by a flour scoop: a stack of loose pages covered in pencil. He turns the top one toward the bulb.

A drawing from floor level. The underside of a counter. A crate of bottles. Two pairs of shoes. A stool going over. An outflung hand. In the corner, small: 1:07. Beside the shoes, in her careful block capitals: EXCUSE ME.
You drew this.
It's the only thing I know how to do with it. If I don't put it on paper it just keeps happening. That's what he said when he came into the bar. "Excuse me." Like a customer.

steps.title: Exactly where it was
steps.quote: Jack sets the page down exactly where it was.

steps.text: Jack sets the page down exactly where it was.
And then in the bar, the man said, "Where is he?" He was waiting for the old man. They were supposed to meet.
Sakai was bringing him something.

steps.title: The stamp
steps.quote: Mara opens her fist. The coin-locker key on its worn tag.

steps.text: Mara opens her fist. The coin-locker key on its worn tag.
This.

steps.title: The tag 114
steps.quote: The number on the worn tag, still legible: 114.

steps.text: Jack takes it. Turns it over under the bulb. The number on the worn tag, still legible: 114.
It's not a station locker. They clear those every three days.
Then what is it?
Somewhere he paid for. For a long time.
He hands it back. She looks surprised.
Keep it. Until I know what it opens. It's safer with you than with me.
Why?
Because nobody knows where you are.

steps.title: She closes her hand
steps.quote: Mara closes her hand around the key.

steps.text: Mara closes her hand around the key. She looks at him properly for the first time.
Is she eating?
What?
Vera. She forgets to eat when she's upset. She just drinks coffee. Is she eating?

steps.title: Last night she had noodles
steps.quote: Jack thinks of the counter at 11:40 p.m.

steps.text: Jack thinks of the counter at 11:40 p.m. The empty bowls.
Last night she had noodles.
Good. Make her eat breakfast. She never eats breakfast.

scenes.title: Breakfast
scenes.heading: INT. TINY BREAKFAST COUNTER, NEAR THE STATION - MORNING
scenes.place: TINY BREAKFAST COUNTER, NEAR THE STATION

steps.text: A coffee counter no wider than a corridor. Six seats, a glass siphon bubbling over a flame, toast cut as thick as a paperback. A CRT on the shelf shows a morning cooking show, sound low. The window is fogged from the inside.
Vera sits with her coat still on and her phone face up beside her, already looking at the door as though the day has started without her.

steps.title: Breakfast
steps.quote: Jack sets a plate down in front of her: thick toast, a boiled egg, a small dish of pickled cabbage that nobody asked for.

steps.title: Breakfast nobody asked for
steps.quote: Jack sets a plate down in front of her

steps.text: Jack sets a plate down in front of her: thick toast, a boiled egg, a small dish of pickled cabbage that nobody asked for.
What's this?
Breakfast.
I don't eat breakfast.
You drink coffee until the afternoon and then you forget to eat.

steps.title: Reporting on me
steps.quote: Has someone been reporting on me?

steps.text: Has someone been reporting on me?
He says nothing. She looks at the plate. She looks at him. She picks up the toast, mostly to end the conversation.
You sound like my sister.

steps.title: You sound like my sister
steps.quote: Jack's hand stops on his cup.

steps.text: Jack's hand stops on his cup.
Vera doesn't see it. She is looking at the cooking show.
She used to stand over me with a plate. Twenty-four years old, bossing me around my own kitchen. She'd have liked you. She likes anyone who's stubborn.
She sounds like she was right.
Was. Is. I keep saying was.
Is.

steps.title: She was hungry
steps.quote: She bites the toast. Chews.

steps.text: She bites the toast. Chews. Her face changes, the way a person's face does when she finds out she was hungry.

steps.title: The cooking show
steps.quote: On the television a chef lifts a lid and steam fills the frame.

steps.text: She eats the egg. She eats the cabbage. On the television a chef lifts a lid and steam fills the frame.
Jack watches her eat, the way he watched her sleep. It is the easiest hour he has spent in twenty years, and he knows exactly what it is costing.
She wipes her fingers on a paper napkin.
Thank you.
For what?

steps.title: For making me
steps.quote: For making me.

steps.text: For making me.
She reaches for her purse. He is already at the till, paying. Too much. The woman behind the counter doesn't mention it.

steps.title: The loop
steps.quote: A green-striped commuter train circling the city.

steps.text: A green-striped commuter train circling the city. Rain on the windows. Afternoon light, grey and soft. The carriage is half empty: schoolkids, an old man asleep, a woman with shopping.

steps.title: Just riding the loop
steps.quote: Vera and Jack sit side by side.

steps.text: Vera and Jack sit side by side. Nowhere to go. Just riding the loop.
Dad used to do this when he couldn't think. Ride the whole loop. An hour. He said Tokyo was a clock and the Yamanote was the second hand.
Did it help?
I don't know. He did it a lot at the end.
The train sways. Her shoulder settles against his.

steps.title: In his palm
steps.quote: She takes his hand without asking and turns it over.

steps.text: She takes his hand without asking and turns it over. The old steel lighter is in his palm; he has been flicking it without knowing.
She takes it. Opens it. Closes it. Opens it.
You don't smoke.
I quit.
When?
Twenty years ago.
And you still carry the lighter.
Habit.
That's not a habit. That's a promise you don't trust yourself to keep.
He looks at her. She has no idea how true that is.

steps.title: Keep it
steps.quote: He closes her fingers around it.

steps.text: She tries to give it back. He closes her fingers around it.
Keep it.
Why?
Because I quit.

steps.title: The lighter
steps.quote: She looks at the lighter in her hand.

steps.title: The second hand
steps.quote: And her head comes to rest on his shoulder, as if it has always belonged there.

steps.text: She looks at the lighter in her hand. Then she puts it in her coat pocket. And her head comes to rest on his shoulder, as if it has always belonged there.
Out of the window, Tokyo circles past. Rooftops. Laundry. Rain.
A small intersection.
Rain.
The crossing signal turns green and the old melody begins to CHIME.

steps.title: The old song
steps.quote: Vera and Jack cross in the rain, laughing at something, sharing his cheap plastic umbrella that's too small for two.

steps.title: Too small
steps.quote: Vera and Jack cross in the rain, laughing at something, sharing his cheap plastic umbrella that's too small for two.

steps.text: Vera and Jack cross in the rain, laughing at something, sharing his cheap plastic umbrella that's too small for two. Her shoulder gets wet. His gets wet. Neither of them cares.
WIDE: two small figures crossing an empty road while the city's old song plays for them.

steps.title: Daylight again
steps.quote: The bar in daylight again. The rubber mat is still there, still too clean.

steps.text: The bar in daylight again. The rubber mat is still there, still too clean. Okada is polishing a glass that is already polished.

steps.title: Okada polishes the glass
steps.quote: Vera comes in without the umbrella this time. Okada sees her and doesn't say we're closed.

steps.text: Vera comes in without the umbrella this time. Okada sees her and doesn't say we're closed.
Mr. Okada. You said he found your daughter.
Okada goes on polishing.

steps.title: She was fifteen
steps.quote: She was fifteen. She went to Osaka with a boy.

steps.text: She was fifteen. She went to Osaka with a boy. Everyone said she was gone. He found her in three weeks. He didn't bring her home. She didn't want to come. He told me where she was, and he told me not to go. Write, he said. Wait.
Was he right?
She has two children now. I hated him for a year.
He sets the glass down.

steps.title: Carries things by himself
steps.quote: He finds things. And then he carries them by himself.

steps.text: He finds things. And then he carries them by himself. I have never seen him put anything down.
Is that a warning?
It's a description.
Vera looks along the counter, to the far end, where his eyes went the first time.
Show me where.

steps.title: The counter flap
steps.quote: Okada lifts the counter flap: the gap between the crates and the ice bin.

steps.text: Okada lifts the counter flap: the gap between the crates and the ice bin.

She goes through. Crouches behind the far end, between the crates and the shelves, exactly where Mara crouched. She sees what Mara saw: the underside of the counter, the crate of empty bottles, the place where the stool went over, the dark screen of the television on the ceiling.

steps.title: She was here
steps.quote: She was here.

steps.text: She was here.
I was in the back. Moving crates. I heard all of it. I stood there with a crate in my arms and I did not move. That is why I gave you the clip. He said "excuse me" when he came in. Like a customer.
Vera stays where she is on the floor.
She would have stayed very still. She has never been still in her life.
People learn.

steps.title: The dead television
steps.quote: Vera looks up at the dead television. Somewhere in the dark glass, her own face.

steps.text: Vera looks up at the dead television. Somewhere in the dark glass, her own face.
For the first time she lets herself think it clearly: her sister saw two men die, and has not called.
Okada takes a card from his apron and sets it on the counter. TOTO SHIMBUN. The journalist's name in katakana: KONDO.
He left it the week before. He said he was meeting someone. He said it would be a good week. I couldn't call them. I couldn't say what I heard.
Vera takes the card.

scenes.title: The sea wall steps
scenes.heading: EXT. FISHING TOWN, BOSO COAST - DAY

steps.text: Grey sea. Grey sky. Rain on the slipway. Boats pulled up on a concrete slipway. A single road of low houses, their paint scoured by salt wind.

steps.title: The sea wall steps
steps.quote: He gets out, pulls up his collar against the wind, and walks.

steps.text: Jack's old car, parked on the sea wall. He gets out, pulls up his collar against the wind, and walks.

scenes.title: The tea she does not want to pour
scenes.heading: INT. MRS. SAKAI'S HOUSE - DAY

steps.text: A small room. A kotatsu table. A television with the sound off. A Buddhist altar in the corner: a new photograph of Sakai, younger, smiling in a way that doesn't suit him.

steps.title: The tea she does not want to pour
steps.quote: MRS. SAKAI (70s), small and hard, pours Jack tea she doesn't want to pour.

steps.text: MRS. SAKAI (70s), small and hard, pours Jack tea she doesn't want to pour.
We haven't lived together in fifteen years. The police already came.
I'm not the police.
Then what are you?
Jack thinks about it.

steps.title: A man a debt
steps.quote: Someone who owes a man a debt.

steps.text: Someone who owes a man a debt. A long time ago. The same kind of debt your husband owed.

steps.title: The altar photograph
steps.quote: She studies him. Then she looks at the photograph on the altar.

steps.text: She studies him. Then she looks at the photograph on the altar.

He started going to temple last year. Him. Temple. He sat there for hours. I thought he'd gone soft in the head. Last month he wrote a letter. In English. Him. He made me check the spelling. To an American girl. When the doctor told him, he said he was glad. He said now he could stop being afraid of the wrong thing.

steps.title: Did he ever pay rent
steps.quote: Did he ever pay rent on something? Somewhere that wasn't his home?

steps.text: Did he ever pay rent on something? Somewhere that wasn't his home?
She looks at him sharply.
Every January. Cash, in an envelope. Twenty years. Even after he left, the receipts kept coming here. He left these here. Maybe on purpose.

steps.title: The receipts
steps.quote: She takes a rubber-banded bundle of receipts from the altar drawer.

steps.text: She takes a rubber-banded bundle of receipts from the altar drawer. Carbon copies, handwritten, yellowed. The top one: KATO RENTAL LOCKERS, UENO.

steps.title: The stamp 114
steps.quote: Jack unfolds it. A rubber stamp, faded. Handwritten: No. 114. Paid in full.

steps.text: Jack unfolds it. A rubber stamp, faded. Handwritten: No. 114. Paid in full.
He looks up. She is watching him with an expression he can't read. Grief, maybe. Or relief.

steps.title: Heavier than me
steps.quote: Whatever it is, it was heavier than me. He carried it longer.

steps.text: Whatever it is, it was heavier than me. He carried it longer.
Rain. Black fields. Jack's old car, one headlight dimmer than the other, the only thing moving for miles.

steps.title: A light ahead
steps.quote: Ahead, a light. A sign on a pole, half its bulbs dead: a roadside inn.

steps.text: Ahead, a light. A sign on a pole, half its bulbs dead: a roadside inn.

Two storeys of weathered wood and a tin roof, set back from the highway behind a gravel lot. A beer vending machine glowing by the entrance. A faded sign. The kind of place that was modern once, in about 1975.
A pickup truck, older than the building's paint, is parked crooked behind it.

steps.title: The only car
steps.quote: Jack pulls into the lot. The only car.

steps.text: Jack pulls into the lot. The only car.

A small, warm, faded room. A pink public payphone on the wall. A glass case of souvenir keyrings nobody has bought in decades. A CRT television on a shelf showing a night baseball game, the crowd murmuring.
MRS. NODA (70s) comes out from the back, drying her hands. MR. NODA (70s) doesn't look away from the baseball.
Just one night?
Just one.

steps.title: Just one night
steps.quote: She hands him a heavy old key on a wooden tag.

steps.text: She hands him a heavy old key on a wooden tag.

steps.title: Upstairs at the end
steps.quote: Upstairs, at the end. The bath is shared, I'm sorry. I'll show you.

steps.text: Upstairs, at the end. The bath is shared, I'm sorry. I'll show you. The light doesn't work properly.

scenes.title: The window swollen shut
scenes.heading: INT. ROADSIDE INN, CORRIDOR AND BATH - CONTINUOUS

steps.title: The back door sticks
steps.quote: She leads him down a narrow wooden corridor.

steps.text: She leads him down a narrow wooden corridor. Past the kitchen: pots, a steel counter, a back door with a bolt.
Kitchen. If you want tea, just take it. The back door sticks. My husband says he'll fix it. He's said so since the Olympics.
Which Olympics?
Exactly.
She opens a door: a small tiled bathroom, a deep wooden tub, one high window over it, fogged with steam and swollen shut in its frame.

steps.title: The window swollen shut
steps.quote: If it's too steamy, the window opens. If you hit it hard enough.

steps.text: If it's too steamy, the window opens. If you hit it hard enough.
Jack notices the window. He notices everything. That is the point of the scene, and nobody in it knows it.

scenes.title: Twenty years of Januaries
scenes.heading: INT. ROADSIDE INN, JACK'S ROOM - NIGHT

steps.text: Tatami. A low table. A thin futon already laid out. Rain loud on the tin roof.

steps.title: Twenty years of januaries
steps.quote: Jack sits at the table with Sakai's receipts spread out in front of him under the lamp.

steps.title: No 114
steps.quote: KATO RENTAL LOCKERS - UENO. No. 114. Twenty years of Januaries.

steps.text: Jack sits at the table with Sakai's receipts spread out in front of him under the lamp. KATO RENTAL LOCKERS - UENO. No. 114. Twenty years of Januaries.
He takes out his phone. No signal.

steps.title: The pink payphone
steps.quote: Mr. Noda asleep in front of the baseball. Jack at the pink payphone, feeding it coins.

steps.text: Mr. Noda asleep in front of the baseball. Jack at the pink payphone, feeding it coins.

steps.title: Come back safe anyway
steps.quote: Vera on the floor with her back against the bed, the apartment dark around her.

steps.text: Vera on the floor with her back against the bed, the apartment dark around her. Her phone rings. Unknown number. She answers fast.
Mara?
It's me.
A beat. Disappointment, then something else.
Where are you? You sound like you're calling from 1985.
The coast. An inn off the highway. The phone is pink.
She almost laughs.
Did you find anything?

steps.title: The receipts in his hand
steps.quote: Jack looks at the receipts in his hand.

steps.text: Jack looks at the receipts in his hand.
Maybe. I'll know tomorrow.
Come back safe.
It's just an inn. There's an old couple and a baseball game.

steps.title: Come back safe
steps.quote: Come back safe anyway.

steps.text: Come back safe anyway.
He hears her breathing on the line. Neither of them hangs up.

steps.title: The coins run out
steps.quote: The coins run out. The line goes dead.
