steps.text: The coins run out. The line goes dead.
Vera looks at the phone. Jack looks at the payphone. Both of them hold on a moment longer than they need to.

scenes.title: The keys are always in it
scenes.heading: INT. ROADSIDE INN, KITCHEN DOORWAY - NIGHT

steps.text: Jack can't sleep. He wanders back down the corridor.

steps.title: The keys are always in it
steps.quote: Mrs. Noda sits on the step outside under the eave, smoking.

steps.text: The kitchen's back door stands open to the rain. Mrs. Noda sits on the step outside under the eave, smoking.

steps.title: Don't tell my husband
steps.quote: Don't tell my husband.

steps.text: Don't tell my husband.
I quit.
Then you'll understand why I don't want him to know.

steps.title: Parked crooked
steps.quote: a muddy yard, a gate onto a farm track, and the old pickup parked crooked across the path.

steps.text: She offers the pack anyway. He shakes his head. He stands in the doorway and looks out: a muddy yard, a gate onto a farm track, and the old pickup parked crooked across the path.
Sorry about the truck. He parks it like he's drunk. He's never drunk. The keys are always in it. Who would steal that?
Jack looks at the truck. He says nothing.
Later. 2 a.m. Rain.
The highway. Empty. Then headlights.

steps.title: Four black sedans
steps.quote: One car. Two. Three. Four. Black sedans, one after another, slowing, turning in, gravel crunching.

steps.text: One car. Two. Three. Four. Black sedans, one after another, slowing, turning in, gravel crunching.

scenes.title: The curtain gap
scenes.heading: INT. ROADSIDE INN, JACK'S ROOM - CONTINUOUS

steps.text: Jack's eyes open in the dark. He has heard the gravel.

steps.title: He has heard the gravel
steps.quote: He goes to the window. Lifts one corner of the thin curtain.

steps.text: He goes to the window. Lifts one corner of the thin curtain.

steps.title: The curtain gap
steps.quote: four black cars in an arc across the lot, headlights on, rain visible only inside the beams.

steps.text: HIS POV THROUGH THE CURTAIN GAP: four black cars in an arc across the lot, headlights on, rain visible only inside the beams. Eight MEN step out, two from each car. Black clothes. Masks. Compact submachine guns held low and easy.
They don't rush. They split without speaking. Two toward the entrance. Two around the back. Two toward the side. Two stay by the cars.
Jack lets the curtain fall.

steps.title: Takes nothing else
steps.quote: He moves fast and quietly: sweeps the receipts into his jacket, pulls on his shoes, takes nothing else.

steps.text: He moves fast and quietly: sweeps the receipts into his jacket, pulls on his shoes, takes nothing else.
Downstairs, the baseball crowd CHEERS on the TV.

steps.title: Were closed
steps.quote: The front door opens. Two masked men step in, weapons up.

steps.text: The front door opens. Two masked men step in, weapons up.
The first is the MASKED LEADER (40s), a man in a plain dark suit, nothing about him to remember. His face stays behind the mask. The man who touched his earpiece in the Kanda rain.
Mr. Noda wakes in his chair. Stares.
We're closed —

steps.title: Behind the counter
steps.quote: Mr. Noda throws himself behind the counter.

steps.text: A burst of suppressed fire into the ceiling. Plaster rains down. Mr. Noda throws himself behind the counter.

steps.title: Staff side
steps.quote: The souvenir case shatters. The CRT keeps playing baseball.

steps.text: The souvenir case shatters. The CRT keeps playing baseball.

scenes.title: Boots below
scenes.heading: INT. ROADSIDE INN, UPSTAIRS CORRIDOR - CONTINUOUS

steps.title: Boots below
steps.quote: Jack at the top of the stairs. He hears boots below. He goes the other way, toward the bath.

steps.text: Jack at the top of the stairs. He hears boots below. He goes the other way, toward the bath.

steps.title: The screens
steps.quote: The paper screens along one wall burst apart in a line of holes.

steps.text: Behind him, a masked man reaches the top of the stairs and fires down the corridor. The paper screens along one wall burst apart in a line of holes.

steps.title: Same wood
steps.quote: Jack is already through the bathroom door.

steps.text: Jack is already through the bathroom door.
Dark. Steam still hanging. Jack climbs onto the edge of the deep tub and hits the swollen window frame with the heel of his hand. Once. Twice. It won't move.
Boots in the corridor.

steps.title: The third time
steps.quote: The third time, he hits it with everything he has. The frame cracks open. Rain pours in.

steps.text: The third time, he hits it with everything he has. The frame cracks open. Rain pours in.
He hauls himself through.

scenes.title: Wet tin
scenes.heading: EXT. ROADSIDE INN, KITCHEN ROOF - CONTINUOUS

steps.title: Wet tin
steps.quote: Jack drops onto it, slides, catches the gutter, and swings down

steps.text: A low slope of wet tin below the bathroom window. Jack drops onto it, slides, catches the gutter, and swings down —
— through the open back door into the kitchen, where Mrs. Noda is crouched on the floor behind the steel counter, rigid with fear.
He grabs her arm, pulls her low toward the pantry, opens it, puts her inside.

steps.title: Stay whatever you hear
steps.quote: Stay. Whatever you hear.

steps.text: Stay. Whatever you hear.
My husband —
I'll get him.
He closes the pantry door on her.
He moves up the corridor toward the lobby, keeping low along the wall.
From the corridor, Jack can see the lobby. One masked man stands in the middle of the room, weapon up, covering the stairs. The other has gone up.

steps.title: A finger to his lips
steps.quote: Jack puts a finger to his lips.

steps.text: Mr. Noda is behind the counter, out of the gunman's line of sight. He sees Jack. Jack puts a finger to his lips.

steps.title: Thank you very much
steps.quote: Jack reaches out and flips the lobby light switch. DARK.

steps.text: Jack reaches out and flips the lobby light switch. DARK.
Only the TV lights the room now: blue, flickering.
The masked man spins and fires toward the corridor. The shots stitch across the wall above Jack's head. One tears through the beer vending machine by the door.
It lights up and CHIMES:
Thank you very much.
The gunman flinches toward the sound.

steps.title: The shoulder
steps.quote: He grabs Mr. Noda by the collar and drags him down the corridor.

steps.text: In that half-second, Jack is across the dark lobby, behind the counter. He grabs Mr. Noda by the collar and drags him down the corridor.

steps.title: It rings
steps.quote: On the wall, the pink payphone starts to RING. No one answers it. It rings and rings.

steps.text: On the wall, the pink payphone starts to RING.
No one answers it. It rings and rings.

steps.title: Clutch each other
steps.quote: The old couple clutch each other in the dark.

steps.text: Jack pushes Mr. Noda into the pantry beside his wife. The old couple clutch each other in the dark.
Jack looks at them.
I'm sorry.
He shuts the door. He goes out the back.

scenes.title: Mud and impacts
scenes.heading: EXT. ROADSIDE INN, BACK YARD - CONTINUOUS

steps.text: Rain. Mud. The farm gate. The pickup truck.
A masked man comes round the side of the building. Sees him.
Jack runs. Gunfire kicks up mud behind him. He dives behind the truck. Bullets punch through the bodywork above his head, through the tailgate, through a wheel.

steps.title: Mud and impacts
steps.quote: He yanks open the driver's door and pulls himself in, flat along the seat.

steps.text: He yanks open the driver's door and pulls himself in, flat along the seat.

steps.title: Come on come on
steps.quote: The keys are in the ignition, exactly where she said.

steps.text: The keys are in the ignition, exactly where she said.
He turns them. The engine coughs. Dies.
The windscreen cracks as a round goes through it.
Come on. Come on.
He turns the key again. The engine catches. Roars.

scenes.title: No need to chase
scenes.heading: EXT. ROADSIDE INN, BACK YARD - CONTINUOUS

steps.title: Through the farm gate
steps.quote: The truck lurches forward and smashes through the farm gate.

steps.text: The truck lurches forward and smashes through the farm gate. Two masked men throw themselves aside. The truck fishtails through the mud onto the farm track, then onto the highway.
The eight men walk out into the lot, one by one, and stand in the headlights of their cars, watching the single red taillight shrink into the rain.

steps.title: No need to chase
steps.quote: They don't chase him. They don't need to.

steps.text: They don't chase him. They don't need to.
The MASKED LEADER touches his earpiece.
He's gone. He has what she gave him.
Behind them, inside the lobby, the pink payphone is still ringing.
Grey light. Empty highway. Rain through the shattered windscreen.

steps.title: Hand starts to shake
steps.quote: Jack drives with one hand. Blood runs from his hairline down the side of his face.

steps.text: Jack drives with one hand. Blood runs from his hairline down the side of his face. His shirt is dark with it at the shoulder.
He looks in the mirror. No one.

steps.title: Soaked and creased
steps.quote: The receipts are still there, soaked and creased.

steps.text: He reaches into his jacket. The receipts are still there, soaked and creased.
He breathes. Only now does his hand start to shake.
Then the thought arrives, and his face changes.
Only two people knew where he was going tonight. He counts them silently.
Ishida. He asked Ishida for the widow's address.
And Vera. He called her from a pink payphone and told her it was just an inn.
He drives on. The wipers beat. He doesn't want to think it. He thinks it anyway.

scenes.title: The model, corrected
scenes.heading: INT. CHAIRMAN'S OFFICE, KUROSE DEVELOPMENT - DAWN

steps.text: The fortieth floor. Glass on three sides. Tokyo spread out below in the rain like a circuit board. The glass walls grey with dawn. Nobody in the leather chairs.

steps.title: The model at dawn
steps.quote: At the plaza's edge sits one small, dark, patched block, out of place among the towers. The Hive.

steps.text: The model of the redevelopment on its long table: glass towers, sponge trees, a broad white plaza. At the plaza's edge sits one small, dark, patched block, out of place among the towers. The Hive.
A man's hand, clean, with an expensive watch, lifts the Hive out of the model and sets it on a tray beside a cup of tea.

steps.title: The hand on the model
steps.quote: The plaza underneath is already finished. Tiny painted people cross it.

steps.text: The plaza underneath is already finished. Tiny painted people cross it.

steps.title: A knock at the door
steps.quote: A knock at the door.

steps.text: A knock at the door. Vera opens it in a sweater, barely awake.
Jack. Soaked. Blood dried down the side of his face.
Oh my God.

steps.title: She pulls him in
steps.quote: She pulls him in.

steps.text: She pulls him in.
A small tiled bathroom. Jack sits on the closed toilet. Vera kneels in front of him with a bowl of warm water and a cloth, cleaning the cut at his hairline.
He watches her face while she works. Very closely. As though he is trying to read something written there.
Who did this?
I don't know.
You don't know?
Two that I saw. Masks. They didn't introduce themselves.

steps.title: Pink water
steps.quote: She wrings out the cloth. Pink water.

steps.title: Pink water
steps.quote: Pink water.

steps.text: She wrings out the cloth. Pink water.
You told me it was just an inn.
It was just an inn.

steps.title: His eyes go to the phone
steps.quote: Jack's eyes go to Vera's phone on the edge of the bath

steps.title: The phone on the bath
steps.quote: where it has sat all night in case Mara calls.

steps.text: Jack's eyes go to Vera's phone on the edge of the bath, where it has sat all night in case Mara calls. He stops.
She looks up and catches him watching her.
What is it?

steps.title: What he was looking at
steps.quote: He doesn't answer.

steps.title: It frightens her
steps.quote: She sees something in his look that she doesn't understand

steps.text: He doesn't answer. He's still watching. Measuring. She sees something in his look that she doesn't understand, and it frightens her more than the blood.
Jack. What!

steps.title: Careful, steady
steps.quote: He looks at her hands: careful, steady, stained pink.

steps.text: He looks at her hands: careful, steady, stained pink. At her face: exhausted, afraid for him.
Whatever he was looking for, it isn't there. It was never there.
Nothing. I'm sorry. Nothing.
She puts a plaster on the cut, very gently. Her hand stays on his face a moment after.
He covers her hand with his.

steps.title: The kiss
steps.quote: And then, without either of them deciding, she kisses him. Or he kisses her. It doesn't matter which.

steps.text: And then, without either of them deciding, she kisses him. Or he kisses her. It doesn't matter which.
It is quiet, and brief, and it changes everything.
When it ends, she rests her forehead against his.
Don't go anywhere else without telling me.
I won't.
When she turns to wring out the cloth, he reaches over and turns her phone face-down.
It is another promise. He is collecting them.

steps.title: The glass office
steps.quote: An old newspaper office. Stacks of paper. Desks jammed together. Televisions on the walls showing three different channels. Nobody under fifty looks up from a screen.

steps.text: An old newspaper office. Stacks of paper. Desks jammed together. Televisions on the walls showing three different channels. Nobody under fifty looks up from a screen.

Vera stands at the door of a glass-walled office at the back, KONDO's card in her hand. HARADA (50s), the editor, grey-haired, sleeves rolled, is finishing a call. She sees the card and ends it without hurry.

steps.title: The photograph on her desk
steps.quote: On her desk, a framed photograph of the journalist from the bar, laughing at an office party.

steps.text: On her desk, a framed photograph of the journalist from the bar, laughing at an office party.
You're not a reporter.
My sister was in that bar.
Harada looks at her for a long time. Then at the photograph. She points at the chair.
We have had a letter from lawyers already. Kondo was six months on the redevelopment money. Who owns what. Whose friends sit on which committee. He never touched a gang in his life.
The police say it's a gang matter.

steps.title: What they are told
steps.quote: The police say what they are told.

steps.text: The police say what they are told.
Did he say who he was meeting?
One o'clock, Kanda, an old man who wanted to talk. He told two people. Me. And a detective.
Which detective?

steps.title: There was no car
steps.quote: There was no car.

steps.text: He didn't say. He said the detective had promised to keep a car nearby. There was no car.
Vera sits very still.
Will you print it?
Print what? A dead man's diary? Bring me something with a name on it.

steps.title: The card on the desk
steps.quote: Vera writes her number on the back of Kondo's card and leaves it on the desk, beside the photograph.

steps.text: Vera writes her number on the back of Kondo's card and leaves it on the desk, beside the photograph.

steps.title: Wedged into the corner
steps.quote: A tiny kiosk wedged into the corner of a shopping arcade.

steps.text: A tiny kiosk wedged into the corner of a shopping arcade. An OLD TOBACCONIST (80s) behind a window full of cigarette cartons and lottery tickets.
Vera holds up the old photograph. The American man, two small girls, the noodle shop sign.
My father worked near here, a long time ago. Do you know this place?
The tobacconist puts on his glasses. Looks. Smiles with all his remaining teeth.

steps.title: Everything is still there
steps.quote: Kaneko's. Of course. In the Hive.

steps.text: Kaneko's. Of course. In the Hive. Not for long, though. They're knocking it all down.
Vera stares at him.
It's still there?
Everything is still there. Until it isn't.

Vera walks through the narrow corridors with the photograph in her hand, looking at everything as though she's trying to remember it. Bare bulbs. Dripping water. The radio repairman's dozen murmuring stations. Daylight falls in thin cold shafts through the steam.

steps.title: He glances up
steps.quote: A RADIO REPAIRMAN at his bench under a bare bulb glances up at her and back down.

steps.text: At a turning she stops, then takes the left without looking, the way you take a stair you've climbed a thousand times. A hand-painted sign for a DENTIST, one flight up. A RADIO REPAIRMAN at his bench under a bare bulb glances up at her and back down. Through a half-open door, an OLD WOMAN watches sumo on a television the size of a bread box.

steps.title: Where a child's hand would reach
steps.quote: Vera puts her hand flat on the wall, low, where a child's hand would reach.

steps.text: Vera puts her hand flat on the wall, low, where a child's hand would reach.
A train passes overhead. The building trembles.
She stops. Turns a corner.
The noodle counter. The sign.

steps.title: They match
steps.quote: She stands there for a long moment, holding the photograph up beside the real thing. They match.

steps.text: She stands there for a long moment, holding the photograph up beside the real thing. They match.

steps.title: The third stool
steps.quote: Lunchtime. Steam. Three customers.

steps.text: Lunchtime. Steam. Three customers.
Vera sits at the counter.
Kaneko turns from the pot, glances at her, and goes on working.
I'm sorry, I don't know what to order. I was here when I was a child. With my father. He always sat here.
She takes the old photograph from her bag and sets it on the counter: the American man, two small girls, the noodle shop sign.

steps.title: She freezes
steps.quote: Kaneko looks at the photograph for a long moment.

steps.text: Kaneko looks at the photograph for a long moment. Then at Vera. She freezes, just for a second.
He always paid too much.
Vera's breath catches.
You remember him?
And you. You ate everything on his plate.

steps.title: Stool three
steps.quote: She sets a bowl of noodles in front of Vera. Vera looks at it. Her eyes fill.

steps.text: She sets a bowl of noodles in front of Vera. Vera looks at it. Her eyes fill.

scenes.title: Three feet away
scenes.heading: INT. THE HIVE, NOODLE SHOP STOREROOM - CONTINUOUS

steps.text: On the other side of the curtain, three feet away.

steps.title: Three feet away
steps.quote: Mara stands pressed against the wall with both hands over her mouth.

steps.text: Mara stands pressed against the wall with both hands over her mouth. She has heard her sister's voice. She is shaking.
Through the thin gap at the edge of the curtain she can see the back of Vera's head.
Mara takes one step toward the curtain. Her hand lifts to it.
She stops.
She thinks of the purse in the rain. Of the two men falling. Of her sister being followed through these corridors.
Her hand drops.

steps.title: Bring her
steps.quote: Vera eats. All of it. She laughs once, at nothing, wiping her eyes.

steps.text: Vera eats. All of it. She laughs once, at nothing, wiping her eyes.
My sister would love this place. She's never seen it. She only knows it from my stories. When I find her, I'll bring her here.

steps.title: The chopsticks stop
steps.quote: Kaneko's chopsticks stop moving in the pot. She doesn't look up.

steps.text: Kaneko's chopsticks stop moving in the pot. She doesn't look up.
Yes. Bring her.

steps.title: Too much
steps.quote: Vera puts money on the counter. Too much.

steps.text: Vera puts money on the counter. Too much. Kaneko notices and says nothing.
Vera goes, lighter than she has been for the whole film.

steps.title: Slides down the wall
steps.quote: Behind the curtain, Mara slides down the wall to the floor.

steps.text: Behind the curtain, Mara slides down the wall to the floor.
Rain. By the Hive's narrow entrance, under a tin awning, a green public payphone. JACK stands at it with the receiver to his ear. It's ringing.
MRS. SAKAI'S HOUSE

steps.title: The kotatsu
steps.quote: The kotatsu.

steps.title: The altar
steps.quote: The altar.

steps.title: Teacup on its side
steps.quote: A teacup on its side on the tatami.

steps.title: The phone rings
steps.quote: The phone rings in the empty room.

steps.text: The kotatsu. The altar. The television on with the sound off. A teacup on its side on the tatami. The phone rings in the empty room.
THE HIVE

steps.title: At the edge of a high place
steps.quote: Vera comes out of the Hive's narrow entrance, glowing.

steps.text: Vera comes out of the Hive's narrow entrance, glowing.
Jack! It's still here. The noodle shop from the photo. It's real. The same woman — she remembered Dad. She remembered me.

steps.title: It rings
steps.quote: Jack keeps the receiver to his ear. It rings.

steps.text: Jack keeps the receiver to his ear. It rings.
And I went to the newspaper. Harada, the editor. She says Kondo told two people about the one o'clock. Her. And a detective, who promised to keep a car nearby.
Later.

steps.title: A detective
steps.quote: Jack. A detective.

steps.text: Jack. A detective.
Later. Please.
It rings. Nobody answers. He hangs up.
When we find Mara, I'm bringing her here. She'll finally see it.
Yes.

scenes.title: I want my sister
scenes.heading: INT. THE HIVE, NOODLE SHOP STOREROOM - NIGHT

steps.title: A new drawing
steps.quote: On the wall beside her, taped up with rice-paper tape: a new drawing, still smudged.

steps.text: The bulb. Mara sits on the futon with her knees pulled up. Her face is swollen from crying. On the wall beside her, taped up with rice-paper tape: a new drawing, still smudged. The noodle counter from behind the curtain. The back of a head.
Jack crouches in front of her.
She was right there. She was right there and I —
You did the right thing.

steps.title: She was so happy
steps.quote: She said she'd bring me here. When she finds me. She was so happy.

steps.text: Did I? She said she'd bring me here. When she finds me. She was so happy.
She wipes her face with the heel of her hand.
If she found this place, other people can.
I know.
Find what it opens. And then this ends. I don't want to hide any more. I want my sister.

steps.title: I want my sister
steps.quote: She takes the key from around her neck, on a shoelace, and puts it in his hand. Its worn tag reads 114.

steps.text: She takes the key from around her neck, on a shoelace, and puts it in his hand. Its worn tag reads 114.
Tomorrow night I'm moving you out of here. Somewhere safe, outside Tokyo. A police car and a house. Someone I trust.
And then?
And then I tell her everything.
Mara looks at him. She believes him.

steps.title: Nine oclock
steps.quote: Parked under an elevated expressway. Rain drumming on the roof. The dashboard glow.

steps.text: Parked under an elevated expressway. Rain drumming on the roof. The dashboard glow.
Ishida behind the wheel. Jack in the passenger seat. Neither looks at the other.
The inn. I heard this morning. Thank God. The widow's file went through the department the day I pulled it. Someone read it. I am looking for him.

steps.title: The side of his face
steps.quote: Jack studies the side of his face. It is the answer he needs. He takes it.

steps.text: Jack studies the side of his face. It is the answer he needs. He takes it.
I have a witness. From the bar.
A pause. Ishida's expression doesn't change at all. That is the tell, and only we know it.
The sister.

steps.title: Just you
steps.quote: I need a safe car. A safe house outside the city. No paperwork. No department. Just you.

steps.text: I need a safe car. A safe house outside the city. No paperwork. No department. Just you.
When?
Tomorrow night.
Ishida nods slowly, as if thinking it through. As if it costs him something.
Nine o'clock. The service road behind the Hive, by the railway pillars. A grey car. My driver. I'll arrange the house myself. And Sakai's thing?

steps.title: Eyes on the rain
steps.quote: Jack turns and looks at him. Ishida keeps his eyes on the rain on the windscreen.

steps.text: Jack turns and looks at him. Ishida keeps his eyes on the rain on the windscreen.
Where else would the Voss girl go? You took me there yourself. Twenty years ago.

steps.title: Hands on the wheel
steps.quote: Jack looks at Ishida's hands on the wheel. He doesn't ask.

steps.text: Jack looks at Ishida's hands on the wheel. He doesn't ask.
I'll bring it to you. When she's safe.
Good. You've done well, Jack. This time you've done well.
Jack looks out at the rain. For the first time in twenty years, he lets himself believe it.

steps.title: The signal is red
steps.quote: The signal is red. Vera and Jack stand at the kerb under his cheap plastic umbrella.

steps.text: The same small intersection as before. The signal is red. Vera and Jack stand at the kerb under his cheap plastic umbrella.
Tomorrow night. Will you have dinner with me?
She looks at him, surprised.
Like a date?
Like a date.
Jack, my sister —
I know. There's something I need to tell you. I want to tell you properly. Not in an office. Not on a train.

steps.title: Properly
steps.quote: She searches his face. Whatever she finds there makes her smile. Properly.

steps.text: She searches his face. Whatever she finds there makes her smile. Properly. For the first time in the film.
Okay.
The old hotel by the station. The lounge. Ten o'clock.
Ten o'clock.

steps.title: Like a date
steps.quote: The signal turns green. The old melody begins to CHIME.

steps.text: The signal turns green. The old melody begins to CHIME.
They cross. She takes his arm.

scenes.title: No questions
scenes.heading: INT. KATO RENTAL LOCKERS, UENO - NIGHT

steps.text: A narrow room under a railway arch, lined floor to ceiling with battered grey steel lockers, each one numbered in fading paint. A single fluorescent tube. A sign in faded letters: MONTHLY. YEARLY. NO QUESTIONS.
At a desk by the door, a CARETAKER (80s) sleeps with his head on a ledger.

steps.title: No questions
steps.quote: Jack opens a locker with Mara's key.

steps.text: Jack opens a locker with Mara's key. Inside: a padded envelope, taped shut. Under it, a small black notebook, water-stained, its cover gone soft with age.

steps.title: The box
steps.quote: In the envelope, a single cassette tape in a cracked plastic case, labelled in a shaking hand: SHIOHAMA.

steps.text: In the envelope, a single cassette tape in a cracked plastic case, labelled in a shaking hand: SHIOHAMA.

steps.title: Daniel voss flyleaf
steps.quote: He opens the notebook. English handwriting. On the flyleaf: DANIEL VOSS.

steps.text: He opens the notebook. English handwriting. On the flyleaf: DANIEL VOSS.
Jack stands very still.
He turns pages. The handwriting grows faster, more anxious. And then a page near the end, and a line underlined twice.
He reads it. We don't see what it says. We see his face.
He closes it. The notebook goes inside his coat. The envelope he carries in his hand.
A train passes overhead. The lockers rattle in their rows, all of them at once, like a room full of doors being tried.

scenes.title: Not another day
scenes.heading: EXT. UENO, UNDER THE RAILWAY ARCHES - NIGHT

steps.text: A row of brick arches with shops in them: shuttered, lit, shuttered. Rain running down the ironwork. Jack comes out of the locker room with his coat buttoned over the notebook and something flat inside it.

steps.title: The sedan waits
steps.quote: At the far end of the arch, a black sedan sits with its lights off and its engine running.

steps.text: At the far end of the arch, a black sedan sits with its lights off and its engine running.
Jack doesn't look at it. He walks.
Behind him, the sedan's lights come on. It follows at walking pace.

steps.title: Through the parlour
steps.quote: He turns into a doorway of noise: a PACHINKO PARLOUR, a wall of steel balls and light and a hundred people staring at their machines.

steps.text: He turns into a doorway of noise: a PACHINKO PARLOUR, a wall of steel balls and light and a hundred people staring at their machines. He walks straight through, between the rows, out through the fire door at the back and into an alley of dripping air conditioners.
He waits. Watches the far end of the alley.

steps.title: They give up
steps.quote: Two men in dark coats run past the mouth of it, scanning, and are gone.

steps.text: Two men in dark coats run past the mouth of it, scanning, and are gone. Behind them, in the street, the sedan crawls along the kerb and stops. Someone inside is speaking into a sleeve. We can't hear it. We can see him give up.
A last train pulls out overhead. The arches shake.
Jack takes the cassette from inside his coat and looks at it, in the light of a vending machine.

steps.title: Not another day
steps.quote: He can't carry it any more. Not another day.

steps.text: He can't carry it any more. Not another day.
Okada's bar. Late. No customers. The CRT television is off.

steps.title: Behind the counter
steps.quote: Jack slides the cassette case across the counter.

steps.text: Jack slides the cassette case across the counter.
Keep this for me. Don't tell anyone. Not the police. Not me, if I ask you with someone standing behind me.

steps.title: The cassette
steps.quote: Then he takes it, lifts the lid of the old cash drawer, removes the tray, and puts the tape underneath.

steps.text: Okada looks at the tape. Then he takes it, lifts the lid of the old cash drawer, removes the tray, and puts the tape underneath.
Behind the counter. Like the girl's clip.
The girl?
He pours Jack a drink. Jack doesn't drink it.
Safe. Tomorrow it'll be over.
You said that about my daughter.
Rain on the window. The last grey light.

steps.title: The top of the wardrobe
steps.quote: Vera stands on a chair and lifts down a flat cardboard box from the top of the wardrobe.

steps.text: Vera stands on a chair and lifts down a flat cardboard box from the top of the wardrobe. Dust on the lid. Her mother's handwriting on the side, in marker: TOKYO.
She opens it on the bed.

steps.title: Wine red. Silk.
steps.quote: Inside, folded in tissue paper that has gone yellow: a dress. Wine red. Silk.

steps.text: Inside, folded in tissue paper that has gone yellow: a dress. Wine red. Silk. The kind of dress a young woman wore to an expensive restaurant in 1990 and never wore again.

steps.title: The wine red dress
steps.quote: Vera holds it up against herself in the mirror. For a moment she is someone else.

steps.text: Vera holds it up against herself in the mirror. For a moment she is someone else. Her mother, maybe.
Through the thin wall, the neighbour's radio begins to play the same old ballad from before: the woman's voice.
LATER:

steps.title: Out of practice
steps.quote: Vera at the small mirror by the window, in the red dress, doing her makeup.

steps.text: Vera at the small mirror by the window, in the red dress, doing her makeup. She is out of practice. She wipes off the lipstick and does it again. Her hands aren't quite steady.
She looks at herself for a long time. She almost looks happy. She doesn't quite trust it.

steps.title: The old steel lighter
steps.quote: Then, after a moment, the old steel lighter.

steps.text: She picks up her bag. Puts in her phone. Then, after a moment, the old steel lighter.

steps.title: Borrowing it
steps.quote: At the door she stops by the umbrella stand. The pale blue umbrella.

steps.text: At the door she stops by the umbrella stand. The pale blue umbrella.
She takes it.
Borrowing it. You'll get it back.
She goes. Through the wall, the song plays on.
An old hotel built in the Showa years for a future that never quite came. Amber light. Brass rails. Deep leather chairs. Bottles glowing behind the bar like a shrine.

steps.title: To almost no one
steps.quote: In the corner, a PIANIST (60s) in a white jacket plays standards, softly, to almost no one.

steps.text: In the corner, a PIANIST (60s) in a white jacket plays standards, softly, to almost no one.
A clock above the bar: 9:58.

steps.title: Shaking the rain
steps.quote: Vera comes in, shaking the rain from the blue umbrella.

steps.text: Vera comes in, shaking the rain from the blue umbrella. People turn to look at her, briefly. She is beautiful and doesn't know where to put her hands.

steps.title: Waiting for someone
steps.quote: She sits at the bar. Leans the blue umbrella against the next stool.

steps.text: She sits at the bar. Leans the blue umbrella against the next stool.
For you?
I'm waiting for someone. A gin and tonic. Please.
She looks at the door.

steps.title: The clock reads ten
steps.quote: The clock: 10:00.

steps.text: The clock: 10:00.

scenes.title: A different clock
scenes.heading: EXT. SERVICE ROAD BEHIND THE HIVE - NIGHT

steps.text: Earlier. The clock is a different clock here: 8:52 on a lit sign above a closed garage.
A narrow road running under the elevated railway. A row of massive concrete pillars. Puddles. One sodium lamp.

steps.title: A different clock
steps.quote: A grey sedan waits beside the pillars, engine running, wipers slow.

steps.text: A grey sedan waits beside the pillars, engine running, wipers slow.

scenes.title: Rice balls for the car
scenes.heading: INT. THE HIVE, NOODLE SHOP STOREROOM - CONTINUOUS

steps.title: Folded in four
steps.quote: The loose pages of the bar, drawn from the floor, she folds in four and puts in the bag with the rest.

steps.text: Mara puts on a borrowed coat. She has a small cloth bag: a toothbrush, the cardigan, the sketchbook pages she tore from the wall, all but the drawings from behind the curtain, which she leaves taped where they are. The loose pages of the bar, drawn from the floor, she folds in four and puts in the bag with the rest.
Kaneko stands in the curtain. She hands Mara a small parcel wrapped in newspaper.
Rice balls. For the car.
Mara takes them. She doesn't know what to say.
Thank you. For —

steps.title: Rice balls for the car
steps.quote: Come back with your sister. Sit on the stools. Both of you. Eat everything.

steps.text: Come back with your sister. Sit on the stools. Both of you. Eat everything.

steps.title: Like a grandmother
steps.quote: Kaneko, unexpectedly, puts a hand on her head. Just for a second. Like a grandmother.

steps.text: Mara bows, too deep, clumsy. Kaneko, unexpectedly, puts a hand on her head. Just for a second. Like a grandmother.
It's time.
Jack leads Mara through the narrow corridors. Bare bulbs. Dripping pipes. The radio repairman looks up from his bench as they pass, and nods.

steps.title: Other lives
steps.quote: Doors open onto other lives. A family watching television. A man asleep. A girl practising the violin, badly.

steps.text: Doors open onto other lives. A family watching television. A man asleep. A girl practising the violin, badly.

steps.title: Vera would love this
steps.quote: Mara looks at all of it as if memorising it.

steps.text: Mara looks at all of it as if memorising it.
Vera would love this.
You can bring her.
When it's over, you'll tell her? Everything?

steps.title: Meeting her at ten
steps.quote: Tonight. I'm meeting her at ten.

steps.text: Tonight. I'm meeting her at ten.
She stops walking. Looks at him.
Meeting her?
For dinner.

steps.title: Her sisters smile
steps.quote: Mara studies him. And then, for the first time, she smiles. A real one. Her sister's smile.

steps.text: Mara studies him. And then, for the first time, she smiles. A real one. Her sister's smile.
Oh. Oh, I see.
It's not —
It is. It's fine. It's good. She deserves someone who looks for things.
A train passes overhead. The building trembles. They walk on.

scenes.title: Position
scenes.heading: EXT. SERVICE ROAD BEHIND THE HIVE - CONTINUOUS

steps.title: Out of the back door
steps.quote: Jack and Mara come out of a narrow back door of the Hive into the rain.

steps.text: Jack and Mara come out of a narrow back door of the Hive into the rain.

steps.title: He opens the rear door
steps.quote: A DRIVER in a dark coat gets out and opens the rear door for them.

steps.text: The grey sedan waits beside the pillars, twenty metres away. A DRIVER in a dark coat gets out and opens the rear door for them. Polite. Professional. He bows slightly as they come.
Jack walks Mara toward it. Halfway there.
Shitsurei shimasu.
He says it the way you would to a passenger.

steps.title: Mara stops dead
steps.quote: Mara stops dead.

steps.text: Mara stops dead.
She has heard those words before. From the floor of a bar, before two shots.
That's them.
What?
That's what he said. Before he shot him. "Excuse me."

steps.title: Into his sleeve
steps.quote: The driver lifts his wrist to his mouth and murmurs into his sleeve

steps.text: The driver lifts his wrist to his mouth and murmurs into his sleeve, very quietly:
Position.

steps.title: Position
steps.quote: Jack looks at the driver. The driver looks at Jack. And in that look, both men understand.

steps.text: Jack looks at the driver. The driver looks at Jack. And in that look, both men understand.

steps.title: Run
steps.quote: Jack shoves Mara back toward the Hive door.

steps.text: Jack shoves Mara back toward the Hive door.
Run!

steps.title: Between the pillars
steps.quote: From the dark between the pillars: muzzle flashes.

steps.text: From the dark between the pillars: muzzle flashes. Suppressed shots, flat and ordinary.

steps.title: Behind the dumpster
steps.quote: Jack draws Mara down behind a dumpster. Rounds clang off the steel.

steps.text: Jack draws Mara down behind a dumpster. Rounds clang off the steel. The driver pulls a weapon from his coat.

steps.title: Five metres, three
steps.quote: Mara breaks for the Hive door. Five metres. Three.

steps.text: Mara breaks for the Hive door. Five metres. Three.
A shot.

steps.title: Through the doorway
steps.quote: She stumbles. Keeps going. Falls through the doorway.

steps.text: She stumbles. Keeps going. Falls through the doorway.

steps.title: The doorframe
steps.quote: Jack goes after her, low, as bullets chew the doorframe above his head.

steps.text: Jack goes after her, low, as bullets chew the doorframe above his head.

steps.title: The bolt
steps.quote: Jack drags the door shut behind him and throws the bolt.

steps.text: Jack drags the door shut behind him and throws the bolt. Pounding on the door. Shots through it, splintering the wood.

steps.title: Holding her side
steps.quote: Mara is on the floor of the narrow passage, her back against the wall.

steps.text: Mara is on the floor of the narrow passage, her back against the wall. She is holding her side. Her hand is dark and wet.

steps.title: His hands over hers
steps.quote: Jack kneels, presses his hands over hers.

steps.text: Jack kneels, presses his hands over hers.
Stay with me. Mara. Stay with me.

steps.title: The windows wake
steps.quote: Lights snap on, one after another, up through the whole building: the thousand windows of the Hive waking.

steps.text: Above them, a window opens. Then another. Lights snap on, one after another, up through the whole building: the thousand windows of the Hive waking.
Outside, a car door slams. An engine revs. Tyres on wet asphalt. Going.
And far away, finally, sirens.

steps.title: All the light
steps.quote: Mara looks up at all the light.

steps.text: Mara looks up at all the light.
Everyone's awake.
Yes. Everyone's awake. Help's coming.

steps.title: Her grip
steps.quote: Mara's hand finds his wrist. Her grip is weak.

steps.text: Mara's hand finds his wrist. Her grip is weak.
Jack.
I'm here.
Tell her I'm sorry.

steps.title: You'll tell her
steps.quote: You'll tell her. Tonight.

steps.text: You'll tell her. Tonight. I'll bring her here, you can —
Tell her.
Doors open along the passage. Faces in the bulb light: the RADIO REPAIRMAN in his vest, the OLD WOMAN from the sumo room, KANEKO running, still in her apron.

steps.title: Drawings in the water
steps.quote: Pages of drawings, soaking in the thin shining stream that runs along the floor.

steps.text: Mara's cloth bag has split open on the floor. Rice balls. A toothbrush. The cardigan. Pages of drawings, soaking in the thin shining stream that runs along the floor.

steps.title: The pages
steps.quote: Kaneko kneels and begins, very carefully, to pick up the pages.

steps.text: While Jack holds Mara, Kaneko kneels and begins, very carefully, to pick up the pages. The old woman kneels beside her and helps.
Her eyes stay on the lights above. Then they stop moving.
Jack doesn't let go of her hand.

steps.title: Everyones awake
steps.quote: She takes off her apron and folds it and places it gently under Mara's head, as though that still matters.

steps.text: Kaneko sinks down beside them in the narrow passage. She doesn't cry. She takes off her apron and folds it and places it gently under Mara's head, as though that still matters.

steps.title: The bulbs swing
steps.quote: A train passes overhead. The bulbs swing.

steps.text: A train passes overhead. The bulbs swing. The whole building trembles, the way it always does.

steps.title: Eleven fifty-two
steps.quote: The clock above the bar: 11:52.

steps.text: The clock above the bar: 11:52.

steps.title: The wait
steps.quote: Vera's gin and tonic sits untouched. The ice has melted. The lime has sunk.

steps.text: Vera's gin and tonic sits untouched. The ice has melted. The lime has sunk.
The pianist plays something slow. The same old ballad from the neighbour's radio, only now on a piano, stripped of its words.
Vera looks at the door. At her phone. No messages.

steps.title: Open. Shut.
steps.quote: She takes out the lighter and turns it over in her fingers. Open. Shut.

steps.text: She takes out the lighter and turns it over in her fingers. Open. Shut.
Another?
No. Thank you.
She almost laughs at herself. She looks down at the red dress. She feels foolish, and then hurt, and then angry.
Her phone RINGS.

steps.title: The screen
steps.quote: She grabs it. The screen: ISHIDA.

steps.text: She grabs it. The screen: ISHIDA.
Her face changes. She answers.
Hello?
Miss Voss. I'm so sorry to call so late.

steps.title: The call
steps.quote: She knows. From his voice, she already knows. She stands up.

steps.text: She knows. From his voice, she already knows. She stands up.
Your sister was found tonight. I'm very sorry. She died a short time ago.
Vera doesn't move. The piano plays on.
She was with Mr. Jack. He had been hiding her for several days, it seems. In the Hive. I'm sorry. I thought you knew.
The phone slowly lowers from her ear.
The pianist plays. The clock ticks. Somewhere a glass is set down.
Vera walks out of the lounge. Not running yet. Walking very carefully, as if the floor might give way.
The blue umbrella stays where she left it, leaning against the empty stool.

steps.title: Vera runs
steps.quote: Vera comes out of the hotel into the rain and starts to run.

steps.text: Vera comes out of the hotel into the rain and starts to run.

steps.title: The street too long
steps.quote: The elevated railway glows at the far end of the street, and she runs at it as if she could still get there in time.

steps.text: The phone is still in her fist, the call still lit on its screen: ISHIDA. She is not running away from anything. She is running toward the one address she has left. The Hive, and wherever they have laid her sister down. The elevated railway glows at the far end of the street, and she runs at it as if she could still get there in time.

steps.title: Not elegantly badly
steps.quote: Not elegantly. Badly. In heels, in the red dress, no coat, no umbrella. Slipping. Stumbling.

steps.text: Not elegantly. Badly. In heels, in the red dress, no coat, no umbrella. Slipping. Stumbling. Stopping for half a second because she can't breathe, then forcing herself on.
Rain plasters her hair to her face. Her mascara runs.
The song comes up under the rain, and she cannot hear it over her own breath. Her heels on wet pavement. Her breath. A car passing, its tyres hissing.
She runs past a vending machine. It glows, indifferent. She keeps going; the machine falls behind her.

steps.title: Through the crossing
steps.quote: Just beyond it, at a crossing, the old melody chimes for her, and she runs through it on red.

steps.text: Just beyond it, at a crossing, the old melody chimes for her, and she runs through it on red.

steps.title: The lost heel
steps.quote: One heel skids. Her ankle turns. The shoe comes off and stays behind in a puddle. She doesn't stop. She runs on in one shoe.

steps.text: One heel skids. Her ankle turns. The shoe comes off and stays behind in a puddle. She doesn't stop. She runs on in one shoe.

scenes.title: The empty street
scenes.heading: EXT. EMPTY STREET UNDER THE TRACKS - NIGHT

steps.title: No one else is here
steps.quote: A row of vending machines, their cold white light the only light, rain falling through it in columns.

steps.text: A long, empty street beside the elevated railway. Shuttered shops. A row of vending machines, their cold white light the only light, rain falling through it in columns. The black road shining like water.
In a city of fourteen million people, no one else is here.
Jack walks out of the dark from the direction of the Hive. His coat is soaked. His hands are dark. He has not washed them.
He sees her at the far end of the street.
He stops under the awning of a closed shop.

steps.title: Twenty metres apart
steps.quote: Vera slows. Stops. Twenty metres apart.

steps.text: Vera slows. Stops. Twenty metres apart.
For a moment neither of them says anything. She is crying, almost silently.
Jack takes one step toward her.
She shakes her head.
Don't.
He stops.
She looks at him. There is something almost childlike in her face now. Not rage. Disbelief. As though she is still hoping he will tell her that what she's heard is wrong.

steps.title: One shoe
steps.quote: She walks toward him. Slowly. One shoe, one bare foot on the wet road.

steps.text: She walks toward him. Slowly. One shoe, one bare foot on the wet road.
You knew.
Jack doesn't answer.
Her face changes. That silence is the answer.

steps.title: One desperate blow
steps.quote: She hits him. Not a big cinematic slap. One desperate blow against his chest with her fist.

steps.text: She hits him. Not a big cinematic slap. One desperate blow against his chest with her fist.
He takes it.
She hits him again. Then again.
You knew where she was.
He says nothing. He can't. Behind his silence is a promise to a dead girl, and the audience knows it, and Vera doesn't.
She hits him again, weaker. And then the anger drains out of her all at once. Her hands just fall.

steps.title: Why didn't you tell me
steps.quote: Why didn't you tell me?

steps.text: Why didn't you tell me?
Jack opens his mouth. Nothing comes.
She was waiting for me.
That line is almost inaudible.
Jack looks away.
And I was waiting for you. And you were with her.
Jack closes his eyes.
And that is when Vera finally breaks. Not screaming. She simply folds. Her knees hit the wet pavement.
Jack drops down instinctively, reaching for her.

steps.title: She holds on
steps.quote: Her hands grab the front of his coat. She holds on.

steps.text: Her hands grab the front of his coat. She holds on. For one second it looks as if she is going to let him hold her.
Then she realises whose coat it is.
She pushes him away.
And sits there, in the rain, in the red dress.
Jack kneels a few feet away. He doesn't touch her again.
WIDE. EXTREME WIDE.

steps.title: Two small figures
steps.quote: Two small figures on a huge, empty, shining street. The vending machines hum. The rain falls through their light.

steps.text: Two small figures on a huge, empty, shining street. The vending machines hum. The rain falls through their light.
Every sound drops away except the rain.

steps.title: The reflection
steps.quote: In the black water beside Vera, her reflection. And in the reflection, for less than a second, the street is slightly different: a shutter open that is closed, a warm light in a window that is dark, and a figure under a pale blue umbrella who could be Mara, or could be no one.

steps.text: In the black water beside Vera, her reflection. And in the reflection, for less than a second, the street is slightly different: a shutter open that is closed, a warm light in a window that is dark, and a figure under a pale blue umbrella who could be Mara, or could be no one.
It is gone.
Vera covers her face with her hands.

steps.title: Nobody looks down
steps.quote: Above them, an elevated train passes, a long ribbon of lit windows.

steps.text: Above them, an elevated train passes, a long ribbon of lit windows. Inside, strangers sleep, read, stare at their phones. Nobody looks down.
Only now does the SCORE enter: sparse and mournful, as if coming from very far away.
The shot holds. Long enough that it becomes hard to watch. There is nothing Jack can say. Nothing that fixes it.

scenes.title: Still frames — what the night left
scenes.heading: INT./EXT. VARIOUS - NIGHT - SERIES OF SHOTS

steps.text: Still frames. No people.

steps.title: The red shoe
steps.quote: A single red high-heeled shoe lying in a puddle on an empty street, rain dimpling the water around it.

steps.text: — A single red high-heeled shoe lying in a puddle on an empty street, rain dimpling the water around it.

steps.title: The empty lounge
steps.quote: The hotel lounge, empty, the chairs up. The pale blue umbrella still leaning against the bar stool.

steps.text: — The hotel lounge, empty, the chairs up. The pale blue umbrella still leaning against the bar stool.

steps.title: The hive shut
steps.quote: The Hive at night, the noodle shop shutter down, its old sign still faintly glowing.

steps.text: — The Hive at night, the noodle shop shutter down, its old sign still faintly glowing.

steps.title: The machine waits
steps.quote: The vending machine on the empty street, humming, lit, waiting for no one.

steps.text: — The vending machine on the empty street, humming, lit, waiting for no one.

steps.title: Static in a window
steps.quote: A small television in a shop window, showing only static.

steps.text: — A small television in a shop window, showing only static.

steps.title: The empty crossing
steps.quote: The signal turns green for no one, and the old melody CHIMES across the wet street, all the way to the end.

steps.text: — The pedestrian crossing from 27 and 62. Empty. The signal turns green for no one, and the old melody CHIMES across the wet street, all the way to the end.
Darkness. Rain on the window.

steps.title: On the floor
steps.quote: Vera sits on the floor with her back against the bed, still in the ruined red dress, mascara dried on her face. One shoe.

steps.title: The number pressed
steps.quote: The phone lights her face. A contact: MOM. She presses it.

steps.text: Vera sits on the floor with her back against the bed, still in the ruined red dress, mascara dried on her face. One shoe. The phone lights her face. A contact: MOM. She presses it.
Far away, in another morning, it's answered.
Vera? Honey?
Vera opens her mouth. Nothing comes.
Vera?
She ends the call. The screen goes dark.

steps.title: The lighter
steps.quote: In her hand, the old steel lighter. She opens it. Closes it. Opens it.

steps.text: In her hand, the old steel lighter.
She opens it. Closes it. Opens it.

steps.title: Cries without a sound
steps.quote: She should throw it away. She holds it against her chest instead, and bends over it, and cries without making a sound.

steps.text: She should throw it away. She holds it against her chest instead, and bends over it, and cries without making a sound.
She still loves him. She hates herself for it.

steps.title: The desk lamp
steps.quote: The desk lamp. Static on the TV. Jack sits in his wet coat at the desk. He still hasn't washed his hands.

steps.text: The desk lamp. Static on the TV. Jack sits in his wet coat at the desk. He still hasn't washed his hands.
On the desk: Daniel Voss's notebook.
He hears her voice. Over and over. Not the words from tonight. The words from the noodle counter at 11:40.
You're the first person I've trusted since she disappeared.

steps.title: The clean envelope
steps.quote: He opens the drawer. Takes out a clean envelope. Takes Sakai's letter from his coat, smooths it once more along its crease, and folds it inside the notebook's cover. Puts the notebook in the envelope.

steps.text: He opens the drawer. Takes out a clean envelope. Takes Sakai's letter from his coat, smooths it once more along its crease, and folds it inside the notebook's cover. Puts the notebook in the envelope.

steps.title: He writes nothing
steps.quote: He picks up a pen to write something on the envelope. He holds it over the paper for a long time.

steps.text: He picks up a pen to write something on the envelope. He holds it over the paper for a long time.
He writes nothing.

scenes.title: No name
scenes.heading: EXT. VERA'S APARTMENT BUILDING, CORRIDOR - DAWN

steps.title: The walkway
steps.quote: Grey light. An open-air walkway along the third floor. Rain dripping from the railing.

steps.text: Grey light. An open-air walkway along the third floor. Rain dripping from the railing.

steps.title: Squared to the door
steps.quote: He sets the envelope on the mat, squares it to the door, and goes.

steps.text: Jack at Vera's door. He doesn't knock. He sets the envelope on the mat, squares it to the door, and goes.
Vera opens her door. She is still in the dress. She hasn't slept.

steps.title: No name
steps.quote: On the doormat: a plain envelope. No name.

steps.text: On the doormat: a plain envelope. No name.
She picks it up. Opens it. The cloth-covered notebook. And tucked inside its cover, a folded sheet of lined paper.

steps.title: Daniel voss
steps.quote: She sees the name inside the cover, and her whole body goes still.

steps.text: She sees the name inside the cover, and her whole body goes still.
DANIEL VOSS.

steps.title: Grey light
steps.quote: Vera sits at the low table in the dawn light. Beside her, the two cups from the beginning of the film, both empty now.

steps.text: Vera sits at the low table in the dawn light. Beside her, the two cups from the beginning of the film, both empty now.
She unfolds the lined paper first.
Careful, laborious English handwriting. "Miss Voss. Your father did not kill himself. I can prove it."

steps.title: Smoothed flat
steps.quote: It is the letter she threw away. Smoothed flat by someone else's hands.

steps.text: It is the letter she threw away. Smoothed flat by someone else's hands.
She understands, all at once, why her sister was in a Kanda backstreet at one in the morning. Mara went to find the truth Vera refused to look at.
She sets the letter down very carefully, beside the empty cups. Then she opens the notebook and turns the pages.

steps.title: Neat, slanted, careful
steps.quote: Her father's handwriting. Neat, slanted, careful.

steps.text: Her father's handwriting. Neat, slanted, careful.
Shiohama. Third visit. The residents say men came in the spring with flowers, and then in the summer with iron bars. The fire began in two places at once. Fires don't do that.

steps.title: Faster
steps.quote: She turns pages. The handwriting grows faster.

steps.text: She turns pages. The handwriting grows faster.
The claim will be paid. Everyone wants it paid. The company, the police, the man who owns the land now. Kurose. Always Kurose.
Pages.
The police have given me a young detective who speaks English. They call him Jack. He's bright. He believes me. We ate noodles at Kaneko's and I told him everything and he wrote it all down.
Vera stops. Reads that line again.

steps.title: Her hand goes to her mouth
steps.quote: Her hand goes to her mouth.

steps.text: Her hand goes to her mouth.

steps.title: Underlined twice
steps.quote: She turns the page. The line we didn't see Jack read, underlined twice.

steps.text: She turns the page. The line we didn't see Jack read, underlined twice.
Today Jack signed the report. Accidental fire. I don't blame him. He is twenty-eight years old and they own his whole life. But I thought, of all of them, he would stand with me.
Vera stares at the page.
I'll go on alone. I've done it before.

steps.title: Almost unrecognisable
steps.quote: The last pages. The handwriting is almost unrecognisable now.

steps.text: The last pages. The handwriting is almost unrecognisable now.

They followed me home again tonight. The girls were asleep. I stood at the door a long time. If something happens to me, it will not be what they say. Tell Vera. When she is old enough. Tell her it will not be what they say.
Vera closes the notebook.
For twenty years she believed her father chose to leave her.

steps.title: Against her chest
steps.quote: She sits in the grey light, holding the notebook against her chest, the way she held the lighter.

steps.text: She sits in the grey light, holding the notebook against her chest, the way she held the lighter.
She has been given back her father and taken Jack away in the same hour. She doesn't know which to feel first.

scenes.title: Where to find them
scenes.heading: INT. POLICE STATION, DETECTIVES' ROOM - DAY

steps.text: Rows of cluttered desks, most of them empty: the shift change. Two young detectives at the far end, heads down over paperwork, too far away to hear. On the wall, the clock that runs a minute fast.
Ishida sits at his desk writing a report in careful longhand.

steps.title: The long room
steps.quote: Jack walks the length of the room. The young detectives glance up and then look away. He hasn't shaved. There is still dried blood in the creases of his knuckles.

steps.text: Jack walks the length of the room. The young detectives glance up and then look away. He hasn't shaved. There is still dried blood in the creases of his knuckles.

steps.title: Ishida doesnt look up
steps.quote: He stops at Ishida's desk. Ishida doesn't look up.

steps.text: He stops at Ishida's desk. Ishida doesn't look up.
Nine o'clock. A grey car. Your driver.
Ishida finishes his sentence. Puts down the pen.
Only you knew.
A long pause.
You told me yourself, Jack. You always tell the wrong person.

steps.title: Hands close
steps.quote: Jack's hands close at his sides. The far end of the room has gone quiet.

steps.text: Jack's hands close at his sides. The far end of the room has gone quiet.
Twenty years ago. Daniel. Was that you?

steps.title: Where to find them
steps.quote: I only ever told people where to find them.

steps.text: I have never killed anyone in my life. I only ever told people where to find them.
Jack looks at him for a long time. Ishida almost seems to want him to.
He doesn't.
Where is it? Sakai's thing.

steps.title: Past the clock
steps.quote: Jack turns and walks away down the long room, past the desks, past the clock.

steps.text: Jack turns and walks away down the long room, past the desks, past the clock.

steps.title: Afraid
steps.quote: Ishida watches him go. For the first time, he looks afraid.

steps.text: Ishida watches him go. For the first time, he looks afraid.

steps.title: The bar in daylight
steps.quote: The bar in daylight. Chairs on the tables. Okada behind the counter.

steps.text: The bar in daylight. Chairs on the tables. Okada behind the counter.

steps.title: The cash drawer
steps.quote: He opens the cash drawer, lifts out the tray, and hands Jack the cassette.

steps.text: He sees Jack's face and his hands, and he doesn't ask. He opens the cash drawer, lifts out the tray, and hands Jack the cassette.

steps.title: Jack holds it
steps.quote: Jack holds it.

steps.text: Jack holds it.
The girl?
Jack can't answer.

steps.title: Without a toast
steps.quote: Then he pours two small glasses and puts one in front of Jack. They drink together, without a toast.

steps.text: Okada closes his eyes. Then he pours two small glasses and puts one in front of Jack. They drink together, without a toast.

steps.title: The newsroom
steps.quote: An old newspaper office. Stacks of paper. Desks jammed together. Televisions on the walls showing three different channels.

steps.text: An old newspaper office. Stacks of paper. Desks jammed together. Televisions on the walls showing three different channels. Nobody under fifty looks up from a screen.
In a glass-walled office at the back: HARADA (50s), the editor, grey-haired, sleeves rolled. On her desk, a framed photo of the JOURNALIST from the bar, laughing at some office party.

steps.title: The tape between them
steps.quote: On the desk between them: an old cassette player, borrowed from somewhere, and the tape.

steps.text: On the desk between them: an old cassette player, borrowed from somewhere, and the tape.

steps.title: Play
steps.quote: Harada presses PLAY.

steps.text: Harada presses PLAY.

steps.title: Twenty years younger
steps.quote: Hiss. Then two men's voices, twenty years younger.

steps.text: Hiss. Then two men's voices, twenty years younger. Sakai's rough. The other one smooth, patient, faintly bored.
There are still people in the building. Old people. They won't sign.
The building must be empty by the end of the month.
And if it isn't?
Then it will be empty in a different way. Don't make me say it more clearly, Sakai. I don't like to repeat myself.

steps.title: Very far away
steps.quote: Harada stops the tape. The newsroom noise outside the glass seems very far away.

steps.text: Harada stops the tape. The newsroom noise outside the glass seems very far away.
That's Kurose.
That's Kurose.
A voice on a twenty-year-old tape. His lawyers will say it's a fake. They'll say Sakai was a gangster with a grudge.
Then you'll need a witness.
She looks at him.

steps.title: Twenty years ago
steps.quote: Twenty years ago I was a police detective.

steps.text: Twenty years ago I was a police detective. An American insurance investigator named Daniel Voss proved the Shiohama fire was arson. I believed him. I was ordered to close the case, and I signed a report saying the fire was an accident. Weeks later he was found dead. I didn't ask any questions.
You understand what you're saying. You'll be named. Your part too.
Start with my part.

steps.title: Her dead reporter
steps.quote: Then she looks at the photograph of her dead reporter on the desk.

steps.text: Harada looks at him for a long moment. Then she looks at the photograph of her dead reporter on the desk. She takes a notebook from her drawer and opens it to a clean page.
From the beginning.

steps.title: Not silent
steps.quote: We watch him through the glass wall of her office, among the busy desks and flickering televisions: a man, for the first time in twenty years, not silent.

steps.text: Jack begins to talk. We don't hear it. We watch him through the glass wall of her office, among the busy desks and flickering televisions: a man, for the first time in twenty years, not silent.

scenes.title: The notebook photocopied
scenes.heading: INT. TOTO SHIMBUN NEWSROOM, CORRIDOR - LATER

steps.title: At the edge of the newsroom
steps.quote: She has never seen him say anything true in that voice.

steps.text: Vera stands at the edge of the newsroom with a plain folder under her arm and her father's notebook in both hands. Through the glass wall of the office at the back, Jack, talking. She can't hear him. She has never seen him say anything true in that voice.
She doesn't go in.

steps.title: The bar of light
steps.quote: A bar of light passes under the page: her father's handwriting, flashing white. Turn. Press. Turn. Press.

steps.text: A YOUNG COPY CLERK at a photocopier lays the notebook open under the lid and presses the button. A bar of light passes under the page: her father's handwriting, flashing white. Turn. Press. Turn. Press.
Harada comes out of the office and pulls the door closed behind her.

steps.title: He hasn't stopped
steps.quote: Two hours. He hasn't stopped.

steps.text: Two hours. He hasn't stopped.
I know. I can see.
Harada watches the pages come out of the machine.
Every page. Then the original goes in the safe downstairs, and nobody touches it. Including you.
It's all I have of him.

steps.title: I will take care of it
steps.quote: Then I will take care of it.

steps.text: Then I will take care of it. Kondo's files were in his desk. Six months of redevelopment money, and Kurose's name in most of it. And the grey car that left the Hive last night was found burnt out in Adachi at dawn. Registered to a security company. The company belongs to Kurose Development. Tomorrow we put it to them for comment. They will refuse to see a reporter.
I'll go.
That is not your job.

steps.title: He'll want to look at me
steps.quote: It isn't yours either. He'll see me.

steps.text: It isn't yours either. He'll see me. He'll want to look at me.
Harada studies her. Then hands her the folder: a stack of photocopies, warm from the machine.

steps.title: The copies
steps.quote: The copies. Not the original.

steps.text: The copies. Not the original.

scenes.title: It's just a face
scenes.heading: INT. CHAIRMAN'S OFFICE, KUROSE DEVELOPMENT - DAY

steps.title: The fortieth floor
steps.quote: The fortieth floor. Rain on the glass. Tokyo grey and endless below.

steps.text: The fortieth floor. Rain on the glass. Tokyo grey and endless below.
Vera sits in a leather chair in front of Kurose's desk. She wears a plain dark coat. A plain folder is on her lap, her hands flat on its cover: photocopies of every page of her father's notebook.
Across from her sits THE CHAIRMAN, KUROSE (70s). Silver hair. A beautiful suit. The stillness of a man who has never had to hurry.

steps.title: He pours her tea himself
steps.quote: Courteous. Curious. He pours her tea himself.

steps.text: Courteous. Curious. He pours her tea himself.
When my secretary said the daughter of Daniel Voss wanted to see me, I didn't believe her.
His English is perfect. Old-fashioned.
He sat where you're sitting. He looked at me the way you are. As if I'd done something.
Did you?

steps.title: Very expensive
steps.quote: Good men are very expensive.

steps.text: To him? I don't remember. Your father was a good man, Miss Voss. I mean that sincerely. There are not many. Good men are very expensive.
Vera doesn't touch the tea.
What is it you want?

steps.title: The envelope on the glass
steps.quote: He takes a plain envelope, thick with cash, from a drawer and lays it on the glass between them. She doesn't look at it.

steps.text: He takes a plain envelope, thick with cash, from a drawer and lays it on the glass between them. She doesn't look at it.
The Toto Shimbun will print tomorrow. They asked me to bring you the chance to reply.
And they sent you.
I said I'd come.
Why?
I wanted to see your face.
And?

steps.title: Just a face
steps.quote: It's just a face.

steps.text: It's just a face.
For the first time, something flickers in him. Not fear. Irritation, perhaps, at being looked at like that.
Vera stands. She holds up a page of the photocopy. Not threatening. Just showing it to him.

steps.title: Every page
steps.quote: My father kept notes. He wrote your name on every page.

steps.text: My father kept notes. He wrote your name on every page. And now I know.
She walks to the door. On her way out, she stops at the model. Where the Hive stood, there's only the white plaza. Tiny painted people cross it.

steps.title: Very clean
steps.quote: It's very clean.

steps.text: It's very clean.
She goes.
Kurose sits still for a moment. Then he presses a button on his desk phone.

steps.title: Follow her
steps.quote: Follow her.

steps.text: Follow her.

scenes.title: Three feet away
scenes.heading: INT. THE HIVE, NOODLE SHOP STOREROOM - NIGHT

steps.title: The storeroom
steps.quote: The bulb. The flour sacks. The futon, folded now.

steps.title: The dried stack
steps.quote: On it, a neat stack of drawings, dried flat, their edges rippled from the wet floor.

steps.text: The bulb. The flour sacks. The futon, folded now. On it, a neat stack of drawings, dried flat, their edges rippled from the wet floor.

steps.title: He can't go home
steps.quote: Jack sits on the floor against the wall.

steps.text: Jack sits on the floor against the wall. He has been hiding here since the newspaper; he can't go home. His face is grey with exhaustion.
The curtain opens. Kaneko.
Someone for you.
She stands aside.
Vera.

steps.title: Neither moves
steps.quote: Jack gets to his feet. Neither of them moves toward the other.

steps.text: Jack gets to his feet. Neither of them moves toward the other.
She asked me to come. Kaneko. She said I should see where Mara was.
In her hands, a small cloth bag with one strap frayed. Kaneko put it there at the door.

She looks around the tiny room. The bare bulb. The flour sacks. And on the wall, taped up with rice-paper tape, pages from Mara's sketchbook: drawings of the noodle counter, but from the inside now. From behind the curtain. The back of a head.

steps.title: Thats me
steps.quote: Vera walks to the wall. Looks at the drawing for a long time.

steps.text: Vera walks to the wall. Looks at the drawing for a long time.
That's me.
She drew it after you left.
She was here. The day I came.
Three feet away.
Vera touches the paper with one finger.
And you told her not to come out.

steps.title: Both wrong
steps.quote: She was protecting you. So was I.

steps.text: She told herself. She was protecting you. So was I.
Ishida called me before it was on any news. He knew exactly where she was.

steps.title: That's mine
steps.quote: Where she'd be, and when. He arranged the car.

steps.text: I told him. Where she'd be, and when. He arranged the car. It was his driver. That's mine.
I told you about the detective. The one who promised a car. You never asked who.
No.

steps.title: Not all right
steps.quote: Vera says nothing for a while. She does not say it's all right.

steps.text: Vera says nothing for a while. She does not say it's all right.
I'm not going to tell you it wasn't yours.
Don't.

steps.title: Excuse me
steps.quote: Two pairs of shoes. A stool going over. A hand.

steps.text: She opens the bag. Folded pages, soft with handling. She smooths one flat on the flour sack: a counter seen from the floor. Two pairs of shoes. A stool going over. A hand. Beside the shoes, in block capitals: EXCUSE ME.
She drew what she saw. All of it.
She never told me she'd kept them.

steps.title: Somebody has to look
steps.quote: I'm taking these to Harada. Somebody has to look at them.

steps.text: I'm taking these to Harada. Somebody has to look at them. I read his notebook.
I know.
He didn't blame you.
I know.
I don't know if I'm as good as he was.
I'm not asking you to be.

steps.title: The bulb swings
steps.quote: Silence. A train passes overhead. The bulb swings.

steps.text: Silence. A train passes overhead. The bulb swings.
And under the train, so quietly it's almost part of it: in the passage outside, a man's voice, murmuring into his sleeve.
Position.

steps.title: Position
steps.quote: Jack's head snaps round. Vera sees his face and understands.

steps.text: Jack's head snaps round. Vera sees his face and understands.
The bulb goes on swinging.
Three hard strikes, iron on iron, run up the pipes overhead. Then again, farther off: a spoon on a radiator, a knuckle on a drainpipe, floor above floor. The Hive is passing it on.

steps.title: Single file
steps.quote: Four masked men move through the narrow corridors in single file, weapons up. The passages are too narrow for anything else.

steps.text: Four masked men move through the narrow corridors in single file, weapons up. The passages are too narrow for anything else.

steps.title: The hive is watching
steps.quote: Doors that stood open close softly, one after another, as they pass. The Hive is watching them.

steps.text: Doors that stood open close softly, one after another, as they pass. The Hive is watching them.
Kaneko lowers the ladle from the old iron water pipe by the stove. Three strikes were all it took: the alarm the Hive has kept for fifty years.

steps.title: The shutter
steps.quote: Kaneko pulls the shutter down with a crash. She turns off the fluorescent tube.

steps.text: Kaneko pulls the shutter down with a crash. She turns off the fluorescent tube.

steps.title: Through the back
steps.quote: Up. Through the back. The stairs by the dentist. Then go through the neighbours. Everyone will open a door.

steps.text: Up. Through the back. The stairs by the dentist. Then go through the neighbours. Everyone will open a door.
They don't know me.
Jack looks at her.
Come with us.

steps.title: Fifty years
steps.quote: I have lived here fifty years. They can come and find me.

steps.text: I have lived here fifty years. They can come and find me.
Go now. They will help you.
She pushes them toward the back.

scenes.title: The main switch
scenes.heading: INT. THE HIVE, RADIO REPAIR SHOP - CONTINUOUS

steps.title: The repairman
steps.quote: The RADIO REPAIRMAN looks up from his bench at the sound of boots in the corridor. He looks at the old fuse box on his wall.

steps.text: The pipes have already told him. The RADIO REPAIRMAN looks up from his bench at the sound of boots in the corridor. He looks at the old fuse box on his wall.

steps.title: The main switch
steps.quote: He reaches up and pulls the main switch.

steps.text: He reaches up and pulls the main switch.
DARK.
In the black, Vera's hand finds the wall, low, where a child's hand would reach. She starts to move. Jack follows the sound of her.
Every bulb in the building goes out at once.

steps.title: Dark
steps.quote: The masked men stop. Flashlights snap on, tight white beams in the narrow corridors, catching dripping pipes, closed doors, laundry, faces at windows that vanish the moment the light touches them.

steps.text: The masked men stop. Flashlights snap on, tight white beams in the narrow corridors, catching dripping pipes, closed doors, laundry, faces at windows that vanish the moment the light touches them.

steps.title: Faces vanish
steps.quote: The Hive knows its own dark. The men don't.

steps.text: The Hive knows its own dark. The men don't.
Pitch black. A narrow concrete stair.

steps.title: By touch
steps.quote: Vera climbs by touch, one hand on the wall.

steps.title: She lets him
steps.quote: Her other hand finds Jack's and pulls him up after her.

steps.text: Vera climbs by touch, one hand on the wall. Her other hand finds Jack's and pulls him up after her.

steps.title: The unlit lighter
steps.quote: Halfway up, she stops. Takes the lighter out of her pocket. Her thumb on the wheel.

steps.text: Halfway up, she stops. Takes the lighter out of her pocket. Her thumb on the wheel.
Below them: boots. A flashlight beam crawls up the wall and falls away.
She puts the lighter back unlit, and climbs.

scenes.title: Through the rooms
scenes.heading: INT. THE HIVE, THROUGH THE ROOMS - CONTINUOUS

steps.title: The roof
steps.quote: It opens before she can knock: the OLD WOMAN from 55.

steps.text: Vera leads them to a door with a sumo match murmuring behind it. It opens before she can knock: the OLD WOMAN from 55.
The old woman's room. A sumo match murmurs on a television nobody is watching. She points across it to the far wall, where a second door stands open.

steps.title: She jumps
steps.quote: A kitchen in the dark, lit by one candle: the FAMILY around the table, the father with the baseball bat across his knees, the children holding the next door wide.

steps.text: Beyond it, another room. A kitchen in the dark, lit by one candle: the FAMILY around the table, the father with the baseball bat across his knees, the children holding the next door wide. Beyond that, the dentist's chair, the dentist with a finger to his lips. A bedroom where the girl with the violin sits up, the instrument held against her chest like a child.
A passage that is really the inside of someone's wardrobe.

steps.title: The barbers shop
steps.quote: Through the wardrobe, a barber's cramped shop.

steps.text: Through the wardrobe, a barber's cramped shop. The BARBER holds the beaded curtain aside with his scissors hand and turns the chair to the wall, so that anyone looking in will see only a man waiting for a haircut.

steps.title: The laundry
steps.quote: Down four steps into a laundry where wet sheets hang in rows.

steps.text: Down four steps into a laundry where wet sheets hang in rows. Two WOMEN part the sheets ahead of them and pin them shut again behind, so that the whole room closes like water over the place they went.

steps.title: The shrine hatch
steps.quote: A shrine room.

steps.text: A shrine room. A GRANDMOTHER lifts the altar cloth and a low hatch opens behind it. She holds the cloth until they are through, then smooths it flat over the candle and the photograph as if nothing had happened.

steps.title: The plank
steps.quote: A plank laid across the gap between two balconies, a balcony bolted onto a balcony.

steps.text: A plank laid across the gap between two balconies, a balcony bolted onto a balcony. Two MEN in vests steady it at both ends, and when the last of them is across, haul it in after them, so that the gap is only a gap.

steps.title: The pipe gallery
steps.quote: A pipe gallery, the pipes ringing softly all around them.

steps.text: A pipe gallery, the pipes ringing softly all around them. A WOMAN raps one pipe once for clear, and the next hand takes it up farther on: the alarm still passing, now telling them which way is safe.

steps.title: The gap
steps.quote: At every door, someone. A hand. A nod. A lantern turned low.

steps.text: At every door, someone. A hand. A nod. A lantern turned low. Nobody speaks. Nobody looks at Vera or at Jack. They pass through other people's lives like water through a wall.
Behind them, each door closes softly. In the passage beyond, a flashlight beam finds each closed door in turn, and stops.
The Hive is closing behind them the way it opened for the masked men, only the other way round.
The last room is in the rear wing, and it is empty: a window over the foot of the viaduct, its shutter open. An iron fire ladder bolted to the wall outside, going down into the dark.

scenes.title: The ladder under the train
scenes.heading: EXT. THE HIVE, REAR WALL BY THE VIADUCT - CONTINUOUS
scenes.place: THE HIVE, REAR WALL BY THE VIADUCT

steps.text: Rain. The rear wall of the low wing, pressed against the concrete viaduct. Vera comes out of the window onto the ladder. Jack after her, pulling the shutter to behind him.

steps.title: The rails sing
steps.quote: Above, a flashlight beam sweeps the window and finds only a closed shutter.

steps.text: Above, a flashlight beam sweeps the window and finds only a closed shutter.
Overhead the rails begin to sing. A light grows at the far end of the viaduct.

A train. It arrives, a roaring wall of noise and wind and lit windows, and under it the two of them go down the ladder, rung by rung, and nobody hears a thing. Passengers inside reading, sleeping, looking at their phones. None of them see.

steps.title: Inches apart
steps.quote: Her hand is in his on the rail. At the bottom she doesn't take it back.

steps.text: Her hand is in his on the rail. At the bottom she doesn't take it back.

steps.title: The walkway is empty
steps.quote: When the last carriage has passed, the ladder is empty.

steps.text: When the last carriage has passed, the ladder is empty.

scenes.title: Until us
scenes.heading: EXT. STREET BELOW THE VIADUCT - MOMENTS LATER

steps.title: Below the viaduct
steps.quote: Vera and Jack step off the last rung of the fire ladder into an empty street. Soaked. Breathing hard.

steps.text: Vera and Jack step off the last rung of the fire ladder into an empty street. Soaked. Breathing hard.
